domains.name: campaign
domains.description: Core operational domain governing the end-to-end advertising campaign lifecycle — from strategy and planning through trafficking, activation, and delivery. Serves as the SSOT for campaign identity, flight dates, objectives, KPIs, targeting parameters, budget allocation, pacing rules, and execution status across all channels and formats.

products.name: campaign
products.description: Master record for an advertising campaign — the authoritative SSOT for campaign identity, objectives, KPIs, flight dates, status, and high-level strategy. Captures campaign name, advertiser/client reference, campaign type (brand awareness, direct response, performance, retention, seasonal, always-on), campaign status (draft, approved, active, paused, completed, cancelled), start and end dates, campaign objective, primary KPI, secondary KPIs, target ROAS, target CPA, target CPM, target CTR, overall budget ceiling, currency, campaign tier, IAB category, campaign brief reference, approval status, approved by, approved date, go-live date, and audit timestamps. Serves as the root entity for all downstream campaign execution, trafficking, and performance data.

products.name: flight
products.description: Represents a discrete time-bounded execution window within a campaign — a campaign flight (also called a campaign burst or wave). Captures flight name, parent campaign reference, flight start date, flight end date, flight status, flight budget allocation, flight objective override, pacing type (even, front-loaded, back-loaded, custom), pacing goal, daypart restrictions, flight priority, channel mix for this flight, and notes. Enables multi-flight campaign structures where a single campaign runs in sequential or overlapping bursts with distinct budgets and targeting parameters. Aligns with Mediaocean Prisma flight-level planning constructs.

attributes.name: frequency_cap

attributes.name: frequency_cap_period

attributes.name: geo_targeting

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking for this flight relative to other flights in the same campaign or portfolio. Higher values indicate higher priority for budget allocation and inventory access.

attributes.name: target_frequency

products.name: line_item
products.description: Granular execution unit within a campaign flight representing a single buyable unit of media — the atomic record of what is being bought, at what price, on which channel, for which audience. The primary unit of media planning and buying execution. Aligns with Google Campaign Manager 360 placement and The Trade Desk ad group constructs.

products.name: budget_allocation
products.description: Unified financial and delivery control record governing how campaign budget is distributed AND how delivery is paced across flights, line items, channels, and time periods. Captures allocation reference, parent campaign reference, parent flight reference, line item reference, channel type, budget period (monthly, weekly, flight), planned budget amount, revised budget amount, committed spend, actual spend to date, remaining budget, currency, budget source (client-approved, agency-estimated), allocation method (percentage, fixed, dynamic), pacing rule name, pacing type (even, accelerated, front-loaded, back-loaded, custom curve), daily impression goal, daily spend cap, weekly impression goal, weekly spend cap, pacing check frequency (hourly, daily), over-delivery action (pause, throttle, alert), under-delivery action (boost, alert), pacing alert threshold percentage, over-delivery tolerance percentage, under-delivery tolerance percentage, auto-optimization enabled flag, optimization algorithm reference, effective date range, last reconciliation date, and reconciliation status. Serves as the single SSOT for budget allocation decisions, delivery pacing strategy, and pacing guardrails — practitioners manage budget and pacing as a unified workflow because pacing cannot be set independently of budget constraints. Subsumes all pacing rule definitions previously modeled separately.

attributes.description: The priority level assigned to this optimization event. Determines the urgency and order of execution when multiple optimizations are queued. Critical optimizations are executed immediately.

attributes.name: rollback_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this optimization was subsequently rolled back or reversed. True if the optimization was undone, False if it remains in effect. Enables tracking of optimization reversals for governance and learning.

attributes.name: rollback_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the optimization was rolled back. Captures the business rationale for reversing the change, such as negative performance impact, client request, or strategic pivot.

attributes.name: rollback_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the optimization was rolled back, if applicable. Null if the optimization has not been reversed. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the source system from which this optimization event was captured. Examples include The Trade Desk, Google Campaign Manager 360, Mediaocean Prisma, or internal optimization platforms.

attributes.name: test_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this optimization is part of a controlled experiment or A/B test. True if the optimization is being tested against a control group, False for standard optimizations.

attributes.name: trigger_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the optimization was triggered. Captures the business rationale, performance threshold breach, or strategic decision that prompted the change.

attributes.name: trigger_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the optimization was triggered manually by a user, automatically by a system algorithm, or by a predefined rule-based condition.

attributes.name: value_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measurement for the previous and new values. Examples include currency code (USD, EUR), percentage (%), CPM (Cost Per Mille), CPC (Cost Per Click), impressions, or dimensionless for categorical changes.

products.name: creative_usage
products.description: This association product represents the usage event between campaign and creative_asset. It captures the deployment and performance of a specific creative asset within a specific campaign context. Each record links one campaign to one creative_asset with attributes that track how, when, and where the asset was used, along with performance metrics specific to that campaign-asset pairing.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, campaigns routinely deploy multiple creative assets across different channels, platforms, and flight periods (e.g., a holiday campaign uses 15 video assets, 30 display banners, and 10 social creatives). Simultaneously, high-performing assets are reused across multiple campaigns - evergreen brand assets, seasonal creative libraries, and compliance-approved templates are deployed in dozens of campaigns over time. The business actively manages creative usage as an operational entity, tracking which assets run where, when they start/end, and their performance metrics per campaign-asset pairing.

attributes.name: creative_usage_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this creative usage record. Primary key.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the campaign in which this creative asset is being used

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the creative asset being used in this campaign

attributes.name: trafficking_order_id
attributes.description: External identifier from the ad server or trafficking system for this specific asset placement (e.g., DCM placement ID, Sizmek ad ID)

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: Media channel where this asset is deployed for this campaign: display, video, social, search, native, email, out-of-home

attributes.name: click_count
attributes.description: Total number of clicks generated by this specific asset within this campaign. Performance metric specific to this campaign-asset pairing.

attributes.name: conversion_count
attributes.description: Total number of conversions attributed to this asset within this campaign. Performance metric specific to this campaign-asset pairing.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when this usage record was created in the system

attributes.name: ctr
attributes.description: Click-through rate percentage for this asset in this campaign. Calculated as (clicks / impressions) * 100.

attributes.name: impression_count
attributes.description: Total number of impressions delivered for this specific asset within this campaign. Performance metric specific to this campaign-asset pairing.

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: Specific platform or publisher where the asset is running (e.g., Facebook, Google Display Network, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Programmatic DSP)

attributes.name: spend_amount
attributes.description: Total media spend allocated to this specific asset within this campaign. Enables asset-level budget tracking and ROI analysis.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when this usage record was last updated

attributes.name: usage_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this creative asset stopped being used in this campaign. Nullable for ongoing usage. May differ from campaign end if assets are rotated out early.

attributes.name: usage_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this creative asset began being used in this campaign. May differ from campaign start if assets are rotated or phased in.

attributes.name: usage_status
attributes.description: Current status of this asset usage within the campaign: active (currently running), paused (temporarily stopped), completed (flight ended), removed (pulled from campaign)

attributes.name: usage_type
attributes.description: Classification of how this asset is being used in the campaign context: primary (main creative), secondary (supporting), test (A/B testing variant), backup (fallback), seasonal (time-bound theme)

products.name: booking
products.description: This association product represents the inventory reservation contract between a line item and a placement. It captures the specific booking terms, delivery commitments, and performance tracking for each line_item-placement pair. Each record links one line item to one placement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific inventory reservation — including booked volumes, negotiated rates, flight dates, and trafficking/delivery status.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, line items routinely book inventory across multiple placements to achieve reach and frequency goals (e.g., a video line item books pre-roll on YouTube, in-stream on Hulu, and CTV inventory on Roku). Simultaneously, high-value placements serve multiple line items from different campaigns, managed through inventory allocation and yield optimization. Media buyers actively create, manage, and monitor these placement bookings as discrete operational units with booking-specific volumes, rates, dates, and delivery tracking.

attributes.name: booking_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this placement booking record. Primary key.

attributes.name: line_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the line item that is booking this placement inventory.

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the placement position being reserved for this line item.

attributes.name: worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who created this placement booking.

attributes.name: booked_clicks
attributes.description: The contracted number of clicks to be delivered for this specific line_item-placement combination.

attributes.name: booked_impressions
attributes.description: The contracted number of impressions to be delivered for this specific line_item-placement combination. This is booking-specific because a line item may book different impression volumes across multiple placements.

attributes.name: booking_code
attributes.description: External business identifier for this placement booking, used in ad server trafficking and billing reconciliation.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this placement booking record was created in the system.

attributes.name: delivery_status
attributes.description: The current delivery performance status for this specific placement booking. Indicates whether this booking is meeting its delivery goals.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date when this placement booking stops serving. May differ from line item flight dates if placements are staggered.

attributes.name: rate_amount
attributes.description: The negotiated unit rate for this specific placement booking. Rate can vary by placement even within the same line item based on placement quality, position, and negotiation.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when this placement booking begins serving. May differ from line item flight dates if placements are staggered.

attributes.name: trafficking_status
attributes.description: The operational status of creative trafficking and ad server setup for this specific placement booking. Tracks readiness at the booking level.

products.name: creative_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of creative assets to line items for media execution. It captures the operational relationship between what is being bought (line item) and what creative content is served (creative asset). Each record links one line item to one creative asset with attributes that govern rotation, scheduling, trafficking, and performance tracking for that specific pairing.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, line items routinely serve multiple creative assets simultaneously through rotation strategies (A/B testing, dynamic creative optimization, sequential messaging). Each creative asset is reused across multiple line items spanning different campaigns, flights, and targeting strategies. The business actively manages creative assignments as operational records with rotation weights, scheduling windows, trafficking status, and performance metrics tracked per line-item-asset pairing.

attributes.name: creative_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this creative assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: assignment_created_by_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who created this creative assignment. Establishes accountability for trafficking decisions.

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the creative asset assigned to this line item

attributes.name: line_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the line item that will serve this creative asset

attributes.name: assignment_created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this creative assignment was created in the system. Audit trail for trafficking workflow.

attributes.name: click_count
attributes.description: The number of clicks generated by this specific creative asset on this specific line item. Performance metric tracked at the assignment level.

attributes.name: conversion_count
attributes.description: The number of conversions attributed to this specific creative asset on this specific line item. Performance metric for conversion-based campaigns.

attributes.name: ctr
attributes.description: Click-through rate for this creative-line item pairing, calculated as (clicks / impressions). Performance metric for creative effectiveness.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date when this creative asset stops serving on this line item. Supports flight-based creative strategies and seasonal messaging.

attributes.name: impression_count
attributes.description: The number of impressions delivered for this specific creative asset on this specific line item. Performance metric tracked at the assignment level.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this assignment record. Supports change tracking and audit.

attributes.name: priority_rank
attributes.description: The priority or sequence order of this creative within the line item's rotation. Used when rotation is not purely weight-based but follows a priority waterfall.

attributes.name: rotation_weight
attributes.description: The percentage or weight assigned to this creative asset within the line item's creative rotation. Used for A/B testing and dynamic creative optimization. Sum of weights across all assignments for a line item typically equals 100.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when this creative asset begins serving on this line item. Enables sequential messaging and time-based creative rotation strategies.

attributes.name: trafficking_status
attributes.description: The operational status of this specific creative-to-line-item assignment in the ad serving platform. Indicates whether the creative has been successfully trafficked and is ready to serve.

attributes.name: view_count
attributes.description: The number of video views or viewable impressions for this specific creative asset on this specific line item. Applicable to video and viewability-measured formats.

products.name: ad_placement_rotation
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment between an ad creative and a specific placement position where it is trafficked to serve. It captures the rotation configuration, delivery schedule, and performance metrics for each ad-placement pairing. Each record links one ad to one placement with attributes that exist only in the context of this trafficking relationship, including rotation weight, delivery window, and impression/click metrics.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, a single ad creative is routinely trafficked to serve across multiple placement positions (e.g., homepage leaderboard, sidebar, mobile banner) to maximize reach and test performance across inventory. Conversely, a single placement position serves multiple different ads through rotation for A/B testing, sequential messaging campaigns, and daypart-specific creative strategies. Ad trafficking teams actively manage these rotation assignments, configuring weights, schedules, and tracking delivery metrics for each ad-placement pairing.

attributes.name: ad_placement_rotation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this ad-placement rotation assignment. Primary key.

attributes.name: ad_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the ad unit being trafficked in this rotation assignment

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the placement position where the ad is served

attributes.name: click_count
attributes.description: Total number of clicks recorded for this ad in this specific placement. Performance metric tracked at the rotation level.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this ad-placement rotation assignment was created in the trafficking system.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when this ad stops serving in this specific placement. Null indicates no end date for this rotation assignment.

attributes.name: impression_count
attributes.description: Total number of impressions delivered for this ad in this specific placement. Performance metric tracked at the rotation level.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this rotation assignment configuration.

attributes.name: rotation_weight
attributes.description: Relative weight for ad rotation when multiple ads are eligible to serve in this placement. Used for A/B testing and creative optimization. Higher weight = higher probability of serving.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when this ad becomes eligible to serve in this specific placement. Allows for daypart-specific or sequential creative strategies.

attributes.name: trafficking_status
attributes.description: Operational status of this specific ad-placement rotation assignment. Indicates whether the rotation has been trafficked to the ad server and is actively serving.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the trafficking specialist who created this rotation assignment.

products.name: campaign_spokesperson
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between campaign and spokesperson. It captures the operational assignment of brand spokespersons to specific advertising campaigns, including their role, media formats, appearance count, compensation, and usage rights. Each record links one campaign to one spokesperson with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific campaign-spokesperson engagement.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, campaigns routinely engage multiple spokespersons across different channels, markets, and creative executions (e.g., a campaign may have a celebrity primary spokesperson for TV, an influencer for social media, and an executive for corporate messaging). Conversely, spokespersons—especially brand ambassadors and executives—participate in multiple campaigns over their contract period. Talent management and legal teams actively manage these assignments as operational records, tracking role, compensation, usage rights, and approval status for each campaign-spokesperson pairing.

attributes.name: campaign_spokesperson_id
attributes.description: Primary key for campaign_spokesperson

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the campaign that this spokesperson is assigned to.

attributes.name: spokesperson_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this campaign-spokesperson assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: appearance_count
attributes.description: Number of times this spokesperson appears or is featured in creative assets for this campaign. Identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of this specific spokesperson assignment to this campaign: pending (awaiting approval), approved (cleared for use), rejected (not approved), expired (approval period ended). Identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this spokesperson's engagement with this campaign ends.

attributes.name: assignment_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this spokesperson's engagement with this campaign begins.

attributes.name: compensation_amount
attributes.description: Compensation amount paid to this spokesperson specifically for this campaign engagement. Identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this campaign-spokesperson assignment record was first created.

attributes.name: media_formats
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of media formats where this spokesperson appears in this campaign (TV, digital, print, radio, social, OOH). Identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this campaign-spokesperson assignment record was last modified.

attributes.name: role_in_campaign
attributes.description: The role this spokesperson plays in this specific campaign: primary (lead spokesperson), supporting (secondary role), featured (guest appearance), testimonial (customer testimonial role). Identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: usage_rights_period
attributes.description: Time period for which the advertiser has rights to use this spokesperson's likeness and content from this campaign (e.g., 12 months, perpetual, campaign duration only). Identified in detection phase relationship data.

products.name: competitive_targeting
products.description: This association product represents the competitive conquest strategy between a campaign and a competitive brand. It captures the specific tactics, share-of-voice targets, and monitoring parameters defined by media planners when a campaign explicitly targets a competitor brand. Each record links one campaign to one competitive brand with attributes that exist only in the context of this competitive targeting relationship.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, campaigns routinely target multiple competitor brands simultaneously through conquest strategies, with each competitor requiring distinct tactics, SOV targets, and budget allocations. Conversely, each competitor brand is targeted by multiple campaigns over time as part of ongoing competitive intelligence and market positioning efforts. Media planners actively manage these competitive targeting relationships as operational entities with specific strategic parameters per campaign-competitor pair.

attributes.name: competitive_targeting_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this campaign-competitive brand targeting relationship. Primary key.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the campaign that is executing the competitive targeting strategy

attributes.name: competitive_brand_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Campaign Competitive Targeting - Competitive Brand Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the competitor brand being targeted by this campaign

attributes.name: budget_allocated_vs_competitor
attributes.description: Portion of campaign budget specifically allocated to competitive tactics against this competitor brand

attributes.name: competitive_response_type
attributes.description: The type of competitive strategy employed against this specific competitor brand in this campaign (e.g., conquest, defensive, comparative advertising, share steal, awareness parity)

attributes.name: competitive_threat_level
attributes.description: Assessment of the competitive threat level this specific competitor brand poses in the context of this particular campaign (may differ from the general threat level in the competitive_brand master record)

attributes.name: counter_strategy_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting the specific counter-strategy, tactics, messaging, and creative approach used to target this competitor brand within this campaign

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this competitive targeting relationship was first created in the system

attributes.name: monitoring_start_date
attributes.description: The date when competitive monitoring and targeting for this specific competitor began within this campaign

attributes.name: share_of_voice_target_vs_competitor
attributes.business_glossary_term: Share of Voice Target vs Competitor
attributes.description: Target share of voice percentage relative to this specific competitor brand. Represents the desired ratio of campaign impressions to competitor impressions in the target market.

attributes.name: targeting_status
attributes.description: Current status of the competitive targeting for this campaign-competitor pair

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this competitive targeting relationship was last modified

products.name: optimization_rule
products.description: Master reference table for optimization_rule. Referenced by optimization_rule_id.

attributes.name: optimization_rule_id
attributes.description: Primary key for optimization_rule

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: The type of action the rule will execute when its conditions are met (e.g., increase bid, decrease bid, pause campaign, resume campaign, adjust budget, rotate creative, exclude placement). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: increase_bid|decrease_bid|pause_campaign|resume_campaign|adjust_budget|rotate_creative|exclude_placement|send_alert|change_targeting — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: action_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the action value (e.g., percentage, absolute currency amount, multiplier, count, impressions, clicks).

attributes.name: action_value
attributes.description: The numeric value associated with the action (e.g., bid adjustment percentage, budget increase amount, frequency cap limit).

attributes.name: applies_to_scope
attributes.description: The level of the campaign hierarchy to which this rule applies (e.g., campaign, ad group, ad, keyword, placement, creative).

attributes.name: auto_apply
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rule automatically applies changes when triggered (true) or requires manual approval (false).

attributes.name: channel_filter
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of advertising channels to which this rule applies (e.g., search, display, social, video, native). Empty means applies to all channels.

attributes.name: condition_logic
attributes.description: The logical expression or criteria that must be met for the rule to trigger. May include thresholds, comparisons, and boolean operators.

attributes.name: cooldown_period_hours
attributes.description: The minimum number of hours that must elapse between consecutive executions of the rule, preventing rapid successive changes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the optimization rule record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: days_of_week
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of days of the week when the rule is active (e.g., Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Empty means applies to all days.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the optimization rule, including its purpose, logic, and intended impact on campaign performance.

attributes.name: device_filter
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of device types to which this rule applies (e.g., desktop, mobile, tablet). Empty means applies to all devices.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date when the optimization rule ceases to be active. Nullable for rules with no defined end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date when the optimization rule becomes active and begins evaluating conditions.

attributes.name: evaluation_window_hours
attributes.description: The time window in hours over which the rule evaluates performance data before triggering an action.

attributes.name: execution_count
attributes.description: The total number of times the optimization rule has been executed since creation.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: How often the rule is evaluated and potentially executed (e.g., real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, on-demand).

attributes.name: geo_filter
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of geographic locations (countries, regions, cities) to which this rule applies. Empty means applies to all locations.

attributes.name: last_executed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the optimization rule was last executed and triggered an action. Nullable if never executed.

attributes.name: max_executions_per_day
attributes.description: The maximum number of times the rule can be executed within a single day, used to prevent over-optimization or excessive changes.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who last modified the optimization rule.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the optimization rule record was last modified.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional notes, comments, or context about the optimization rule.

attributes.name: notification_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether notifications should be sent when the rule is triggered and executed.

attributes.name: notification_recipients
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses or user identifiers who should receive notifications when the rule executes.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Numeric priority level of the rule, used to determine execution order when multiple rules apply to the same campaign or ad group. Lower numbers indicate higher priority.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique code for the optimization rule, used for reference across systems and reporting.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the optimization rule, describing its purpose or function.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the optimization rule, indicating whether it is active, inactive, draft, archived, suspended, or pending approval.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the optimization rule by its functional category (e.g., budget pacing, bid adjustment, frequency capping, dayparting, geo-targeting, creative rotation).

attributes.name: threshold_metric
attributes.description: The performance metric or key performance indicator (KPI) that the rule monitors (e.g., cost per acquisition, click-through rate, return on ad spend, impressions, conversions).

attributes.name: threshold_operator
attributes.description: The comparison operator used to evaluate the threshold condition (e.g., greater than, less than, equal to, greater or equal, less or equal, not equal).

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The numeric threshold value that triggers the rule when the monitored metric crosses this boundary.

attributes.name: time_of_day_end
attributes.description: The end time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour) when the rule is active for dayparting rules. Nullable if not applicable.

attributes.name: time_of_day_start
attributes.description: The start time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour) when the rule is active for dayparting rules. Nullable if not applicable.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: The version number of the optimization rule, incremented with each modification to track rule evolution.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who created the optimization rule.

attributes.name: parent_optimization_rule_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on optimization_rule (parent_optimization_rule_id)

products.name: optimization_algorithm
products.description: Master reference table for optimization_algorithm. Referenced by optimization_algorithm_id.

attributes.name: optimization_algorithm_id
attributes.description: Primary key for optimization_algorithm

attributes.name: replacement_algorithm_id
attributes.description: Reference to the successor algorithm that replaces this one, if deprecated.

attributes.name: algorithm_category
attributes.description: Technical category describing the underlying approach of the algorithm (machine learning, rule-based, heuristic, or hybrid).

attributes.name: algorithm_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier code for the algorithm, used in system integrations and reporting.

attributes.name: algorithm_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the optimization algorithm (e.g., 'Budget Pacing', 'Bid Optimization', 'Creative Rotation').

attributes.name: algorithm_type
attributes.description: Classification of the optimization algorithm by its primary function within campaign execution.

attributes.name: applicable_channels
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of advertising channels where this algorithm can be applied (e.g., 'display,video,social,search,audio').

attributes.name: applicable_formats
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of creative formats supported by this algorithm (e.g., 'banner,video,native,rich_media').

attributes.name: average_performance_lift_percent
attributes.description: Historical average performance improvement percentage achieved by this algorithm compared to baseline or control campaigns.

attributes.name: confidence_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum confidence level required for the algorithm to make optimization decisions, expressed as a decimal (0.0 to 1.0).

attributes.name: cost_per_use
attributes.description: Cost incurred per execution or application of the algorithm, if usage-based pricing applies.

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who created the algorithm record.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the algorithm record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: deprecation_reason
attributes.description: Business justification for deprecating or retiring the algorithm, if status is deprecated or inactive.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the algorithm's purpose, methodology, and use cases within campaign optimization.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: Web address linking to detailed technical and business documentation for the algorithm.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the algorithm was or will be retired from active use, null if currently active with no planned retirement.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the algorithm became available for use in campaign optimization.

attributes.name: is_proprietary
attributes.description: Indicates whether the algorithm is proprietary intellectual property developed in-house (true) or licensed from external vendor (false).

attributes.name: learning_rate
attributes.description: Rate at which the algorithm adapts to new data and performance signals, typically between 0.0001 and 1.0.

attributes.name: license_type
attributes.description: Type of licensing arrangement for the algorithm (perpetual, subscription, usage-based, open source, or proprietary).

attributes.name: lookback_window_hours
attributes.description: Time window in hours that the algorithm considers when analyzing historical performance data for optimization decisions.

attributes.name: minimum_budget_amount
attributes.description: Minimum campaign budget amount required for the algorithm to be applied, if applicable.

attributes.name: minimum_data_points
attributes.description: Minimum number of data observations required before the algorithm begins making optimization decisions.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the algorithm model, following semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0, v2.3.1).

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified the algorithm record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the algorithm record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: optimization_objective
attributes.description: Primary business goal the algorithm is designed to achieve (e.g., maximize clicks, minimize CPA, maximize ROAS).

attributes.name: performance_benchmark_metric
attributes.description: Primary key performance indicator (KPI) used to measure and benchmark the algorithm's effectiveness (e.g., 'CTR improvement %', 'CPA reduction %').

attributes.name: requires_minimum_budget
attributes.description: Indicates whether the algorithm requires a minimum campaign budget threshold to function effectively.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the optimization algorithm indicating its availability for campaign use.

attributes.name: supports_cross_channel
attributes.description: Indicates whether the algorithm can optimize across multiple advertising channels (display, video, social, search).

attributes.name: supports_programmatic_guaranteed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the algorithm is compatible with programmatic guaranteed deal types.

attributes.name: supports_real_time_bidding
attributes.description: Indicates whether the algorithm can operate in real-time bidding environments with sub-second decision requirements.

attributes.name: update_frequency_minutes
attributes.description: Frequency in minutes at which the algorithm recalculates and applies optimization adjustments.

attributes.name: vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the technology vendor or provider of the algorithm, if sourced externally.

attributes.name: evolved_from_optimization_algorithm_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on optimization_algorithm (evolved_from_optimization_algorithm_id)

domains.name: client
domains.description: Authoritative SSOT for all advertiser identity, account hierarchy, and relationship data. Manages client profiles, brand portfolios, account teams, contact information, business segments, relationship history, and CRM records for both direct advertisers and agency-managed accounts. Supports Account Management and Client Services.
domains.references: 4As Client Management Standards / Salesforce CRM Account Model

products.name: advertiser
products.description: Master record for every advertiser (direct client or agency-managed brand) that the agency serves. Captures authoritative identity including legal entity name, trading name, industry vertical (IAB taxonomy), business segment, holding company affiliation, CRM account ID (Salesforce), ERP customer number (SAP), tax identifiers (VAT/EIN), incorporation jurisdiction, credit terms, payment terms, preferred currency, account status (prospect, active, dormant, churned), account tier, and all engagement preferences (preferred communication channels, reporting cadence, invoice delivery method, language preference, time zone, approval workflow preferences, GDPR/CCPA data sharing consent flags). Also stores structured address records (registered office, billing address, shipping address, regional offices) with address type, full postal details, country (ISO 3166), geocoordinates, and validation status. This is the SSOT for advertiser identity, commercial configuration, engagement preferences, and physical/mailing addresses across the entire data model.

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the advertiser record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the advertiser master data product. Role: MASTER_PARTY.

attributes.name: client_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_segment. Business justification: Advertisers are classified into strategic business segments. The advertiser table currently has 'business_segment' as a STRING field, which should be normalized to a FK reference to the client_segment

attributes.name: account_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the advertiser account. Drives workflow routing, reporting segmentation, and CRM pipeline management. 'prospect' = pre-contract; 'active' = live campaigns; 'dormant' = no recent activity; 'churned' = relationship ended; 'suspended' = temporarily on hold.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: account_tier
attributes.description: Commercial tier classification of the advertiser based on revenue contribution, strategic importance, and engagement level. Determines service level, dedicated account team assignment, and reporting cadence. Aligns with agency tiering models used in account management.

attributes.name: address_validation_status
attributes.description: Indicates the validation status of the advertiser's billing address against a postal address verification service. 'validated' = confirmed deliverable; 'unvalidated' = not yet checked; 'failed' = address could not be verified; 'pending' = verification in progress. Used in SAP S/4HANA and Mediaocean Prisma billing workflows.
attributes.references: Universal Postal Union; SAP S/4HANA FI; ISO 19160

attributes.name: approval_workflow_type
attributes.description: Defines the creative and campaign approval workflow configuration for this advertiser. 'single_approver' = one designated approver; 'multi_approver' = sequential or parallel approval chain; 'auto_approve' = pre-authorized for specific asset types. Configured in Workfront proofing module.

attributes.name: ccpa_consent_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Data Sharing Consent Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the advertiser has opted in to data sharing under CCPA regulations. True = data sharing permitted; False = opt-out or not applicable. Applicable for California-based advertisers and campaigns targeting California consumers. Drives NAI and TAG compliance controls.
attributes.references: CCPA; NAI Code of Conduct; TAG; FTC

attributes.name: churn_date
attributes.description: The date on which the advertiser's account was marked as churned (relationship ended). Populated only when account_status = 'churned'. Used for churn analysis, win-back campaign targeting, and P&L impact reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the advertiser master record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Represents the audit trail creation event. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for data lineage, audit compliance, and record lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2); IAB Tech Lab; Databricks Lakehouse

attributes.name: credit_terms
attributes.description: The agreed payment credit terms for this advertiser, defining the number of days after invoice date by which payment is due. Configured in SAP S/4HANA AR and Mediaocean Prisma for billing workflows. Drives cash flow forecasting and P&L management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI; Mediaocean Prisma; GAAP

attributes.name: crm_account_code
attributes.description: The unique account identifier assigned to this advertiser in Salesforce CRM (Sales Cloud). Serves as the cross-system join key between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the CRM system of record for account management and client services.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: ein
attributes.description: The US federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) assigned by the IRS to the advertiser. Used for US tax reporting, W-9 compliance, and financial reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA. Applicable for US-incorporated entities.
attributes.references: IRS EIN Standards; FTC Advertising Practices; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: erp_customer_number
attributes.description: The customer master number assigned to this advertiser in SAP S/4HANA (FI/AR module). Used for billing, accounts receivable, and financial reconciliation processes. Links advertiser identity to financial transactions.

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Data Sharing Consent Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the advertiser has provided explicit consent for data sharing and processing under GDPR. True = consent granted; False = consent not granted or withdrawn. Mandatory for EU-based advertisers and any data processing involving EU data subjects. Drives data governance controls.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6; GDPR Article 7; EASA; IAB TCF 2.0

attributes.name: holding_company_name
attributes.description: The name of the parent holding company or corporate group to which this advertiser belongs (e.g., WPP, Publicis, Omnicom client-side equivalent). Used for consolidated billing, conflict-of-interest checks, and group-level revenue reporting.

attributes.name: iab_industry_vertical
attributes.description: The advertiser's primary industry vertical classified using the IAB Content Taxonomy. Used for audience targeting, competitive analysis, Share of Voice (SOV) reporting, and media planning segmentation. Examples: 'Automotive', 'Financial Services', 'Consumer Packaged Goods'. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product aligned to IAB Content Taxonomy v3.0]
attributes.references: IAB Content Taxonomy v3.0; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: incorporation_jurisdiction
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the advertiser's legal entity is incorporated. Used for regulatory compliance, tax treatment, and contract law determination. Examples: 'US', 'GB', 'DEU'.

attributes.name: invoice_delivery_method
attributes.description: The preferred method by which invoices are delivered to the advertiser. Drives automated invoice dispatch workflows in SAP S/4HANA and Mediaocean Prisma. 'edi' = Electronic Data Interchange for enterprise clients with automated AP systems.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma; SAP S/4HANA FI; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: is_agency_managed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this advertiser is managed through an intermediary agency relationship (True) or is a direct client of the agency (False). Determines billing structure, IO (Insertion Order) routing, and account team assignment in Mediaocean Prisma and Salesforce CRM.

attributes.name: language_preference
attributes.description: The advertiser's preferred language for communications, reports, and invoices, expressed as an IETF BCP 47 language tag (e.g., 'en-US', 'fr-FR', 'de-DE'). Drives localization in Salesforce Marketing Cloud and report generation workflows.
attributes.references: IETF BCP 47; GDPR Article 12; Salesforce CRM

attributes.name: legal_entity_name
attributes.description: The full registered legal name of the advertiser as recorded with the relevant incorporation authority. Used for contracts, invoices, and regulatory filings. Maps to Salesforce CRM Account Name (legal) and SAP S/4HANA customer master legal name.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab; FTC Advertising Practices; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: managing_agency_name
attributes.description: Name of the intermediary agency managing this advertiser's account, if is_agency_managed is True. Used for IO routing, commission calculations, and agency-of-record (AOR) tracking in Mediaocean Prisma and Salesforce CRM.

attributes.name: onboarding_date
attributes.description: The date on which the advertiser was formally onboarded as a client of the agency. Marks the start of the commercial relationship. Used for tenure calculations, anniversary-based QBR scheduling, and cohort analysis in analytics workflows.

attributes.name: payment_terms
attributes.description: The agreed payment method/instrument for this advertiser's invoices. Distinct from credit_terms (which defines timing); this defines the payment channel/instrument. Configured in SAP S/4HANA and Mediaocean Prisma for financial reconciliation.

attributes.name: preferred_comm_channel
attributes.description: The advertiser's preferred channel for day-to-day account communications and notifications. Used to route alerts, campaign updates, and approval requests in Salesforce CRM and Workfront project management workflows.

attributes.name: preferred_currency
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code representing the advertiser's preferred billing and reporting currency (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'). Used in Mediaocean Prisma for media billing and SAP S/4HANA for invoicing and financial reconciliation.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Mediaocean Prisma; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: The primary email address of the advertiser's main point of contact at the client organization. Used for campaign communications, reporting delivery, and account management correspondence. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Contact object.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the advertiser's primary point of contact at the client organization. Used in account management, QBR preparation, and client services workflows. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Contact object.

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for the advertiser's main point of contact. Used for urgent campaign communications and account management. Stored in E.164 international format. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Contact object.

attributes.name: registered_office_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country where the advertiser's registered office is located. May differ from billing address country. Used for regulatory compliance, GDPR/CCPA applicability determination, and legal jurisdiction.

attributes.name: reporting_cadence
attributes.description: The agreed frequency at which performance reports and analytics dashboards are delivered to the advertiser. Drives automated report scheduling in Google Campaign Manager 360 and analytics workflows. Aligns with QBR (Quarterly Business Review) planning.
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: The advertiser's primary operational time zone expressed as an IANA Time Zone Database identifier (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Used for scheduling campaign flights, reporting cadence, and meeting coordination in Workfront and Salesforce CRM.
attributes.references: IANA Time Zone Database; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: trading_name
attributes.description: The brand or 'doing business as' (DBA) name under which the advertiser operates commercially. May differ from the legal entity name. Used in campaign documentation, media plans, and client-facing materials.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the advertiser master record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2); IAB Tech Lab; Databricks Lakehouse

attributes.name: vat_number
attributes.description: The advertiser's Value Added Tax (VAT) registration number issued by the relevant tax authority. Required for EU/UK invoicing compliance and cross-border tax treatment. Stored for financial reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA FI module.
attributes.references: EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; EASA; GDPR Article 4

products.name: advertiser_hierarchy
products.description: Defines the parent-child organizational hierarchy among advertiser entities — holding company, subsidiary, brand, and sub-brand relationships. Supports multi-level account trees for large conglomerates (e.g., WPP, Publicis clients) where billing, reporting, and campaign attribution must roll up through corporate structures. Tracks hierarchy type (holding, subsidiary, brand portfolio), effective dates, and consolidation flags.

attributes.name: advertiser_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each advertiser hierarchy relationship record in the silver layer. Serves as the primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: child_advertiser_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the child advertiser entity in the hierarchy (e.g., subsidiary, brand, or sub-brand). References the advertiser entity that sits one level below the parent in the corporate tree.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Salesforce CRM Account Hierarchy

attributes.name: parent_advertiser_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent advertiser entity in the hierarchy (e.g., holding company or parent subsidiary). References the advertiser entity that sits one level above the child in the corporate tree.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Salesforce CRM Account Hierarchy

attributes.name: primary_root_advertiser_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the ultimate holding company or top-level entity in the advertiser corporate tree. Enables direct roll-up to the conglomerate level for consolidated billing, SOV analysis, and enterprise reporting without traversing the full hierarchy path.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Salesforce CRM Account Hierarchy

attributes.name: agency_commission_rate
attributes.description: The negotiated agency commission rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.1500 for 15%) applicable to media buys placed on behalf of the child entity within this hierarchy. Stored at the hierarchy level to support tiered commission structures for holding company clients in Mediaocean Prisma.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma; 4As Commission Standards; SAP S/4HANA CO

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the account management or finance authority who approved the establishment or modification of this hierarchy relationship. Required for governance and SOW compliance in client services workflows.
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: The date on which this hierarchy relationship was formally approved by the designated account management or finance authority. Distinct from the effective start date — approval may precede the operational effective date.
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud

attributes.name: billing_consolidation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether invoices and media spend for the child entity are consolidated and billed through the parent entity. Distinct from the general consolidation flag — specifically governs Mediaocean Prisma billing workflows and Insertion Order (IO) aggregation.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma; SAP S/4HANA FI; IAB Insertion Order Standards

attributes.name: change_reason
attributes.description: Categorized reason code explaining why this hierarchy relationship record was created or last modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change management reporting for account management teams during corporate restructuring events. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: acquisition|divestiture|rebranding|restructuring|correction|initial_setup|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; SAP S/4HANA CO

attributes.name: consolidation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child entity's spend, impressions, and campaign performance metrics should be financially consolidated into the parent entity's reporting and P&L. Critical for holding company clients where subsidiary budgets roll up to a master account in SAP S/4HANA CO.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO; Mediaocean Prisma; ANA Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code of the primary operating jurisdiction for this hierarchy relationship. Used to apply correct regulatory reporting requirements (GDPR, CCPA, FTC), tax treatment in SAP S/4HANA, and local media buying rules.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GDPR; CCPA; FTC Advertising Practices Division

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this advertiser hierarchy relationship record was first created in the system. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation anchor for data governance and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; Databricks Lakehouse Delta Lake Audit Standards

attributes.name: crm_hierarchy_code
attributes.description: The native account hierarchy relationship identifier from Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud. Enables bi-directional synchronization between the lakehouse silver layer and the CRM system of record for account management and client services workflows.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the billing and financial consolidation currency applicable to this hierarchy relationship (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'). Governs how media spend and agency fees are consolidated in Mediaocean Prisma and SAP S/4HANA FI.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA FI; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: data_sharing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child advertiser entity has provided consent for audience data and campaign performance data to be shared with the parent entity in this hierarchy. Critical for GDPR and CCPA compliance when consolidating audience insights across corporate structures.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6; CCPA; IAB Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF) 2.0

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this parent-child hierarchy relationship ceases to be operationally effective. Nullable for open-ended relationships. Supports temporal hierarchy versioning when corporate structures change due to divestitures or rebranding.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which this parent-child hierarchy relationship became or becomes operationally effective. Used to enforce temporally accurate billing roll-ups and campaign attribution when corporate structures change (e.g., acquisition effective date).
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: hierarchy_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business code uniquely identifying this parent-child hierarchy relationship. Used in Mediaocean Prisma and Salesforce CRM for cross-system reconciliation and billing roll-up references.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma; Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud

attributes.name: hierarchy_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the business context, rationale, or special conditions of this parent-child hierarchy relationship. Captures nuances such as regional carve-outs, brand licensing arrangements, or joint venture structures not fully expressed by the type and role fields.

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of the child advertiser entity within the corporate account tree, where level 1 represents the ultimate holding company. Enables multi-level roll-up queries for consolidated P&L and campaign reporting across conglomerates such as WPP or Publicis.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Salesforce CRM Account Hierarchy

attributes.name: hierarchy_name
attributes.description: Human-readable label describing this specific parent-child hierarchy relationship (e.g., 'Unilever > Dove Brand Portfolio'). Used in account management dashboards, QBR presentations, and client services reporting for clear identification of the relationship.
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Materialized slash-delimited path string representing the full ancestry chain from the root holding company to the current child node (e.g., '/HoldCo/SubsidiaryA/BrandX'). Supports efficient subtree queries and lineage tracing in Databricks without recursive CTEs.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Databricks Lakehouse Best Practices

attributes.name: hierarchy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the parent-child hierarchy relationship. Drives whether the relationship is used for active campaign attribution, billing consolidation, and reporting roll-ups in Mediaocean Prisma and Google Campaign Manager 360.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: hierarchy_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the parent-child relationship within the advertiser corporate structure. Determines how billing, reporting, and campaign attribution roll up through the account tree. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: holding_company|subsidiary|brand_portfolio|brand|sub_brand|division — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Data Standards; 4As Account Management Standards

attributes.name: industry_sector
attributes.description: The IAB Content Taxonomy industry sector classification of the child advertiser entity within this hierarchy (e.g., 'Consumer Packaged Goods', 'Automotive', 'Financial Services'). Supports audience segmentation, competitive SOV analysis, and Nielsen Ad Intel competitive monitoring.
attributes.references: IAB Content Taxonomy 3.0; Nielsen Ad Intel

attributes.name: is_primary_hierarchy
attributes.description: Indicates whether this relationship represents the primary (canonical) hierarchy path for the child advertiser entity. When an entity belongs to multiple hierarchy trees (e.g., matrix structures), this flag identifies the authoritative roll-up path for billing and consolidated reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Sales Cloud; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: market_region
attributes.description: The geographic market region in which this hierarchy relationship is operationally active (e.g., 'North America', 'EMEA', 'APAC'). Determines applicable regulatory frameworks (GDPR, CCPA), media buying practices, and regional account team assignments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: North America|EMEA|APAC|LATAM|MEA|Global — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ownership_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of ownership the parent entity holds in the child entity (0.00–100.00). Used to determine proportional financial consolidation thresholds and to classify the relationship as majority-owned, minority-owned, or affiliated for P&L reporting in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI; ANA Financial Reporting Standards; IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements

attributes.name: prisma_hierarchy_code
attributes.description: The native account hierarchy identifier from Mediaocean Prisma used for media planning, buying, and billing roll-up. Supports reconciliation between the lakehouse and Prisma for consolidated media spend reporting across the advertiser corporate tree.

attributes.name: relationship_role
attributes.description: Describes the commercial or legal role of the child entity relative to the parent within the hierarchy (e.g., wholly-owned subsidiary vs. franchise vs. joint venture). Informs contract and billing treatment in SAP S/4HANA and Mediaocean Prisma.
attributes.references: ANA Account Governance Standards; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: reporting_consolidation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether campaign performance data (impressions, clicks, CTR, ROAS) for the child entity rolls up into the parent entity's consolidated reporting dashboards in Google Campaign Manager 360 and The Trade Desk. May differ from billing consolidation in matrix account structures.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360; The Trade Desk; MRC Measurement Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this hierarchy relationship record was originally sourced or is mastered. Supports data lineage tracking and conflict resolution when the same hierarchy is maintained across multiple systems.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards; IAB Tech Lab Data Standards

attributes.name: sov_rollup_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child entity's media spend and impressions should be included in the parent entity's Share of Voice (SOV) calculations for competitive analysis in Nielsen Ad Intel and Comscore. Enables accurate conglomerate-level SOV reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Ad Intel; Comscore; MRC Measurement Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this advertiser hierarchy relationship record was most recently modified. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks silver layer.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; Databricks Lakehouse Delta Lake Audit Standards

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version counter for this hierarchy relationship record. Incremented each time the hierarchy definition is modified (e.g., ownership percentage change, status update). Supports optimistic concurrency control and audit trail reconstruction.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Delta Lake; 4As Data Governance Standards

products.name: client_brand
products.description: Represents an individual brand owned by an advertiser. A single advertiser may manage multiple brands (e.g., Unilever owns Dove, Axe, Lipton). Captures brand name, brand code, category, sub-category, brand tier, launch date, brand status, and the owning advertiser. Serves as the SSOT for brand identity referenced by campaigns, creative assets, and media plans. Distinct from the brand domain's brand strategy and positioning entities.

attributes.name: client_brand_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier for the parent brand when this brand is a sub-brand or brand extension (e.g., Dove Men+Care is a sub-brand of Dove). Enables brand hierarchy navigation for portfolio reporting and consolidated media planning.
attributes.references: ANA Brand Management Guidelines; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: brand_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to brand.brand_profile. Business justification: Links client's brand entity to master brand profile for centralized brand guidelines, positioning, tone, visual identity, and compliance rules. Essential for campaign planning, creative briefing, and

attributes.name: client_brand_advertiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent advertiser (client) who owns this brand. A single advertiser may own multiple brands (e.g., Unilever owns Dove, Axe, Lipton).
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM - Account Object; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: client_brand_campaign_manager_advertiser_id
attributes.description: The advertiser/brand identifier assigned within Google Campaign Manager 360 for ad serving, trafficking, and reporting. Required for reconciling impression delivery data and click-through reporting back to the brand.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Advertiser Configuration; IAB Ad Serving Standards

attributes.name: worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal employee designated as the primary account manager responsible for this brand relationship. Sourced from Workday HCM and Salesforce CRM Service Cloud.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM - Account Team; 4As Account Management Standards

attributes.name: annual_media_budget
attributes.description: The total approved annual media spend budget allocated to this brand in the base currency. Used for budget pacing, media plan authorization, and Profit & Loss (P&L) reporting in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA - CO Budget Management; 4As Financial Management Standards; ANA Budget Benchmarking

attributes.name: brand_category
attributes.description: Primary product or service category the brand competes in (e.g., Personal Care, Food & Beverage, Automotive, Financial Services). Aligns with IAB Content Taxonomy for audience targeting and competitive analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Personal Care|Food & Beverage|Automotive|Financial Services|Technology|Retail|Healthcare|Entertainment|Travel|Other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Content Taxonomy 3.0; Nielsen Ad Intel - Category Classification

attributes.name: brand_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric short code uniquely identifying the brand across operational systems including Google Campaign Manager 360, Mediaocean Prisma, and The Trade Desk. Used for trafficking, billing, and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Advertiser/Brand Trafficking; Mediaocean Prisma - Brand Code

attributes.name: brand_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the brand's identity, value proposition, target audience, and key differentiators. Used by account teams, creative teams, and media planners to ensure brand-consistent execution.
attributes.references: 4As Account Management Standards; ANA Brand Management Guidelines

attributes.name: brand_name
attributes.description: The official commercial name of the brand as recognized in the market (e.g., Dove, Axe, Lipton). Used as the primary human-readable identifier across campaigns, creative assets, and media plans.
attributes.references: IAB Data Standards; ANA Brand Management Guidelines

attributes.name: brand_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the brand record. Controls whether the brand is eligible for campaign assignment, media planning, and creative production. 'pending_launch' indicates a brand approved but not yet publicly launched.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM - Account Status; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: brand_tier
attributes.description: Strategic positioning tier of the brand within the advertiser's portfolio, indicating relative market positioning and investment priority. Drives media budget allocation, creative production standards, and account team resourcing.
attributes.references: ANA Brand Management Guidelines; 4As Account Management Standards

attributes.name: budget_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the brand's annual media budget (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency financial reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA and Mediaocean Prisma.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA - FI Currency Configuration

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the brand record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for data governance and lineage tracking.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: crm_brand_code
attributes.description: The brand's unique identifier in Salesforce CRM (Sales Cloud / Marketing Cloud). Enables cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the operational CRM system of record.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM - Account/Brand Object; Internal System Integration Standards

attributes.name: dam_folder_code
attributes.description: The folder or collection identifier in Workfront DAM (Digital Asset Management) where all creative assets for this brand are stored. Enables direct navigation from brand record to associated creative library.
attributes.references: Workfront DAM - Digital Asset Management; IAB VAST/VPAID Creative Standards

attributes.name: data_privacy_classification
attributes.description: Privacy classification governing data collection and audience targeting practices for this brand. 'children' applies COPPA/GDPR-K restrictions. 'sensitive' applies enhanced consent requirements under GDPR Article 9 and CCPA. Drives audience data usage policies in the DMP/CDP.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9; CCPA Section 1798.100; COPPA; FTC Advertising Practices Division; NAI Code of Conduct

attributes.name: digital_advertising_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the brand is approved and configured for digital advertising including programmatic, paid search (PPC/SEM), and social media. Controls eligibility for The Trade Desk DSP activation and Google Campaign Manager 360 trafficking.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; TAG Certified Against Fraud

attributes.name: discontinuation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the brand was officially discontinued or retired from the market. Null for active brands. Used to enforce data governance rules preventing new campaign assignments to discontinued brands.
attributes.references: ANA Brand Management Guidelines; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: guidelines_url
attributes.description: URL pointing to the brand's official style guide and creative guidelines document stored in Workfront DAM or Adobe Creative Cloud. Used by creative teams to ensure brand-consistent asset production.
attributes.references: Workfront DAM - Asset Management; Adobe Creative Cloud - Brand Guidelines; 4As Creative Standards

attributes.name: iab_category_code
attributes.description: The IAB Content Taxonomy category code assigned to the brand (e.g., IAB1, IAB7-25). Used for programmatic audience targeting on The Trade Desk, brand safety controls, and contextual advertising alignment.
attributes.references: IAB Content Taxonomy 3.0; TAG Brand Safety Standards

attributes.name: is_house_brand
attributes.description: Indicates whether this brand is an agency house brand or proprietary brand (True) versus a client-owned advertiser brand (False). Affects revenue recognition, conflict-of-interest checks, and P&L attribution in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: 4As Agency Financial Standards; SAP S/4HANA - CO Profit Center Accounting

attributes.name: launch_date
attributes.description: The date on which the brand was officially launched in the market. Used for brand age calculations, anniversary campaign planning, and historical performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: nielsen_brand_code
attributes.description: The brand identifier assigned by Nielsen Ad Intel for competitive monitoring, audience measurement, and Gross Rating Point (GRP) tracking. Enables competitive spend benchmarking and Share of Voice (SOV) analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Ad Intel - Brand Classification; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: operating_markets
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes representing all markets where the brand is actively sold and advertised. Used for multi-market campaign planning, regulatory compliance scoping, and global media buying via The Trade Desk.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; IAB Data Standards; EASA Cross-Border Advertising Standards

attributes.name: portfolio_rank
attributes.description: Numeric rank of the brand within the advertiser's portfolio based on strategic importance and revenue contribution (1 = highest priority). Used for resource allocation, account team staffing, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) prioritization.
attributes.references: ANA Brand Management Guidelines; 4As Account Management Standards

attributes.name: primary_channel
attributes.description: The primary media channel through which the brand predominantly advertises. Drives default media planning templates in Mediaocean Prisma and channel-specific KPI frameworks. OOH = Out-of-Home.
attributes.references: IAB Channel Classification; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards

attributes.name: primary_market_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the brand's primary operating market (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Drives regulatory compliance requirements (GDPR, CCPA), media planning geography, and reporting currency selection.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GDPR Article 3; CCPA Section 1798

attributes.name: prisma_brand_code
attributes.description: The brand identifier used in Mediaocean Prisma for media planning, buying, billing, and financial reconciliation. Ensures accurate budget allocation and invoice matching at the brand level.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma - Brand/Product Code; 4As Media Billing Standards

attributes.name: programmatic_eligible
