attributes.name: cpm_rate
attributes.description: Negotiated Cost Per Mille (CPM) — the cost per 1,000 ad impressions for this scheduled placement. Primary pricing metric for digital and programmatic media. Used for rate card benchmarking and reconciliation.
attributes.references: IAB CPM Pricing Standards; Mediaocean Prisma — Rate Card Module

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this media schedule record was first created in the source system. Provides the audit creation anchor for the record lifecycle and supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Audit Trail; Google Campaign Manager 360 — Change History

attributes.name: creative_rotation_type
attributes.description: Instruction governing how multiple creative assets are rotated across scheduled impressions — even (equal distribution), weighted (percentage-based), sequential (ordered), or optimised (performance-driven). Trafficked into Google Campaign Manager 360.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 — Creative Rotation Settings; IAB Trafficking Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the net and gross cost amounts on this media schedule (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Enables multi-currency media buying and financial consolidation.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI Currency Configuration

attributes.name: daypart
attributes.description: Nielsen standard daypart classification indicating the time-of-day segment in which the ad is scheduled to air. Drives audience composition, CPM pricing, and GRP/TRP calculations. Values follow Nielsen daypart definitions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: early_morning|daytime|early_fringe|prime_access|prime|late_news|late_night|overnight|weekend — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Standard Daypart Definitions; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned three-digit numeric code identifying the Designated Market Area (DMA) for broadcast and local media scheduling. Enables standardised geographic audience measurement and GRP/TRP reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Code Registry; MRC Geographic Standards

attributes.name: flight_end_date
attributes.description: The last calendar date on which ads are scheduled to air or deliver under this media schedule. Defines the closing boundary of the campaign flight period.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Flight Dates; IAB Campaign Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: flight_start_date
attributes.description: The first calendar date on which ads are scheduled to air or deliver under this media schedule. Defines the opening boundary of the campaign flight period.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Flight Dates; IAB Campaign Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: frequency_cap
attributes.description: Maximum number of times a unique user or household may be served this ad within the defined frequency cap period. Controls ad fatigue and audience experience. Trafficked into Google Campaign Manager 360 and The Trade Desk.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 — Frequency Cap Settings; IAB Frequency Capping Standards

attributes.name: frequency_cap_period
attributes.description: Time window over which the frequency cap applies — hour, day, week, month, or lifetime of the campaign. Works in conjunction with frequency_cap to define the full frequency capping rule.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 — Frequency Cap Settings; IAB Frequency Capping Standards

attributes.name: gross_cost
attributes.description: Gross cost of the scheduled media buy before agency commission deduction, expressed in the billing currency. Represents the full rate card value billed by the media vendor.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Cost Module; SAP S/4HANA FI; 4As Agency Commission Standards

attributes.name: is_makegood
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this schedule record represents a make-good — a compensatory placement provided by the media vendor to offset an under-delivery or missed airing from a prior schedule. Critical for reconciliation and vendor performance tracking.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Make-Good Workflow; 4As Make-Good Standards

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this media schedule record was most recently modified in the source system or the Silver Layer. Used for incremental data loading, change detection, and audit trail. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Audit Trail; Google Campaign Manager 360 — Change History

attributes.name: market_name
attributes.description: Geographic market or Designated Market Area (DMA) where the media will air or be delivered — e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'National'. Used for local vs. national media planning and GRP/TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Market Definitions; Mediaocean Prisma — Market Module

attributes.name: net_cost
attributes.description: Net cost of the scheduled media buy after agency commission and negotiated discounts, expressed in the billing currency. Used for budget management, P&L reporting, and financial reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Cost Module; SAP S/4HANA FI; 4As Agency Commission Standards

attributes.name: pod_position
attributes.description: Requested or guaranteed position of the ad within a commercial break pod for broadcast TV, radio, and CTV/OTT channels. First and last pod positions command premium pricing. Null for non-broadcast channels.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Broadcast Scheduling; Nielsen Ad Intel

attributes.name: preemptible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this scheduled placement can be preempted by a higher-paying advertiser. Preemptible spots are typically priced lower than guaranteed placements. Relevant for broadcast and premium digital inventory.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Broadcast Scheduling; Broadcast Standards and Practices

attributes.name: schedule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name assigned to this media schedule record, typically reflecting the campaign flight, channel, and market (e.g., 'Q3_BrandLaunch_PrimeTV_NYC'). Used for trafficking and reporting identification.

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number for this schedule, as assigned by the media planning system (Mediaocean Prisma) or trafficking system (Google Campaign Manager 360). Used for cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Schedule Reference; Google Campaign Manager 360

attributes.name: scheduled_grp
attributes.description: Total Gross Rating Points (GRP) planned for this media schedule, representing the sum of ratings across all scheduled airings. GRP = Reach % × Frequency. Used for broadcast media planning and audience delivery measurement.
attributes.references: Nielsen GRP Measurement Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: scheduled_impressions
attributes.description: Total number of ad impressions contracted and scheduled for delivery under this media schedule record for the defined flight period. Used for pacing, delivery tracking, and reconciliation against actuals.
attributes.references: MRC Impression Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: scheduled_trp
attributes.description: Total Target Rating Points (TRP) planned for this media schedule, measuring GRP delivery against a specific target audience demographic. TRP is the audience-qualified subset of GRP used for precision media planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen TRP Measurement Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: scheduled_units
attributes.description: Number of discrete ad units (spots, insertions, or placements) scheduled for the flight period — applicable to broadcast (spots), print (insertions), and OOH (faces/panels). Distinct from impressions which measure audience exposure.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Unit Scheduling; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: source_system_ref
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system — Google Campaign Manager 360 placement ID or Mediaocean Prisma schedule line number. Enables traceability and reconciliation back to the system of record.

attributes.name: trafficking_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for trafficking instructions, special placement requirements, or operational notes associated with this media schedule — e.g., 'Run adjacent to news content only', 'Avoid competitor adjacency'. Sourced from Google Campaign Manager 360 trafficking comments.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 — Trafficking Notes; IAB Trafficking Standards

attributes.name: trafficking_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this media schedule in the trafficking workflow. Tracks progression from initial planning through creative assignment, trafficking into ad server, live delivery, and completion or cancellation. Sourced from Google Campaign Manager 360. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_creative|trafficked|live|paused|completed|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 — Trafficking Workflow; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: vehicle_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific media vehicle (publisher, network, station, or platform) where the ad will be delivered — e.g., 'NBC Primetime', 'New York Times Digital', 'Spotify', 'Clear Channel OOH'. Sourced from Mediaocean Prisma publisher library.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma — Publisher/Vehicle Library; IAB Seller.json

products.name: trafficking_instruction
products.description: Transactional record capturing ad trafficking instructions issued to ad servers and media vendors for creative asset delivery. Captures instruction type (new, revision, cancellation), placement reference, creative asset reference, ad server (Google Campaign Manager 360), VAST/VPAID tag URL, click-through URL, impression tracking pixels, viewability tags, brand safety parameters, trafficking date, trafficker name, and instruction status (pending, sent, confirmed). Represents the operational event of dispatching creative to media.
products.reference: Trafficking — Google Campaign Manager 360 / VAST / VPAID

attributes.name: trafficking_instruction_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each ad trafficking instruction record issued to an ad server or media vendor. Serves as the primary key for this transactional entity. ROLE: TRANSACTION_HEADER.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: ad_format_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to media.ad_format. Business justification: trafficking_instruction currently has ad_format as a STRING attribute. Trafficking instructions specify the ad format for delivery to ad servers (e.g., 300x250 Banner, VAST 4.0 Video). This FK normali

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.segment. Business justification: Trafficking instructions configure ad server targeting parameters for specific audience segments. Ad ops teams require explicit segment linkage to set up DMP/DSP integrations, frequency caps, and audi

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent advertising campaign under which this trafficking instruction is issued. Provides campaign-level context for reporting and performance attribution.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Campaign Management; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the creative asset (banner, video, rich media, etc.) being dispatched via this trafficking instruction. Identifies the specific creative unit to be served at the designated placement.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Creative Management; IAB Digital Creative Guidelines

attributes.name: media_insertion_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Insertion Order (IO) authorizing the media buy associated with this trafficking instruction. Provides contractual and financial context for the ad delivery.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma - IO Management; IAB Standard Terms and Conditions for Internet Advertising

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media placement for which this trafficking instruction is issued. Links the instruction to the specific ad unit, position, and publisher property where the creative will be delivered.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Placement Management; IAB Ad Unit Guidelines

attributes.name: parent_instruction_trafficking_instruction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original trafficking instruction that this record revises or cancels. Enables lineage tracking across instruction versions and supports audit of changes to creative delivery parameters.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Versioning; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: sow_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.sow. Business justification: Trafficking is a deliverable service often specified in SOWs with defined SLAs. Linking instructions to SOWs enables service-level tracking, supports billing for trafficking services, and validates sc

attributes.name: trafficker_worker_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to talent.worker. Business justification: Trafficking instructions must track who created and sent them for accountability, revision tracking, and issue resolution. Essential for audit trails and operational handoffs. Replaces denormalized tr

attributes.name: ad_server
attributes.description: Name of the ad serving platform to which this trafficking instruction is dispatched. Identifies the technology stack responsible for delivering the creative asset to the designated placement. Primary system is Google Campaign Manager 360.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Serving; IAB Ad Serving Guidelines; MRC Digital Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: ad_server_placement_code
attributes.description: The unique placement tag or code assigned by the ad server (e.g., Google Campaign Manager 360 placement ID) that maps this instruction to the correct ad unit within the ad serving platform. Used for trafficking reconciliation.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Placement Tagging; IAB Ad Unit Guidelines

attributes.name: brand_safety_provider
attributes.description: Name of the third-party brand safety and suitability verification provider applied to this trafficking instruction. Ensures ad creative is served only in brand-appropriate content environments per TAG and GARM standards.
attributes.references: TAG (Trustworthy Accountability Group) Brand Safety Standards; GARM Brand Safety Floor; IAB Brand Safety Guidelines

attributes.name: brand_safety_segment
attributes.description: Specific brand safety content category or segment classification applied to this instruction (e.g., 'exclude adult content', 'exclude fake news', 'GARM Floor'). Defines the content adjacency restrictions enforced during ad delivery.
attributes.references: TAG Brand Safety Standards; GARM Brand Safety Floor; IAB Content Taxonomy

attributes.name: click_through_url
attributes.description: The destination URL to which users are redirected upon clicking the served ad creative. Must be validated and approved prior to trafficking. Critical for campaign performance tracking and landing page attribution.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Click Tracking; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines; FTC Advertising Practices

attributes.name: confirmed_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the ad server or media vendor confirmed receipt and acceptance of the trafficking instruction. Used for SLA compliance measurement and operational reporting.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Audit; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this trafficking instruction record was first created in the system. Provides the audit trail creation marker for data governance and lineage tracking.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity; IAB Data Governance Guidelines

attributes.name: creative_size
attributes.description: Pixel dimensions of the creative asset being trafficked, expressed as width x height (e.g., 300x250, 728x90, 160x600). Must conform to IAB standard ad unit sizes. Used for placement compatibility validation.
attributes.references: IAB Standard Ad Unit Portfolio; Google Campaign Manager 360 - Creative Specifications

attributes.name: daypart_schedule
attributes.description: Day-of-week and time-of-day scheduling parameters defining when the ad creative should be served (dayparting). Expressed as a structured schedule string (e.g., 'Mon-Fri 08:00-20:00'). Used to optimize delivery timing per media plan.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Daypart Scheduling; Mediaocean Prisma - Media Planning

attributes.name: delivery_end_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which ad creative delivery is to cease per this trafficking instruction. Aligns with the media plan flight end dates and insertion order terms.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma - Flight Scheduling; Google Campaign Manager 360 - Campaign Scheduling; IAB Standard IO Terms

attributes.name: delivery_start_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which ad creative delivery is to commence per this trafficking instruction. Aligns with the media plan flight dates and insertion order terms.
attributes.references: Mediaocean Prisma - Flight Scheduling; Google Campaign Manager 360 - Campaign Scheduling; IAB Standard IO Terms

attributes.name: device_targeting
attributes.description: Device type targeting parameters specifying which device categories the ad creative should be served on (e.g., desktop, mobile, tablet, Connected TV (CTV), or all devices). Aligns with media plan targeting specifications.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Device Targeting; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: frequency_cap_impressions
attributes.description: Maximum number of times the ad creative may be served to a single unique user within the defined frequency cap period. Controls ad exposure and prevents overexposure to individual users.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Frequency Capping; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: frequency_cap_period
attributes.description: Time window over which the frequency cap impressions limit applies. Defines the reset interval for the per-user impression count (e.g., no more than 3 impressions per day).
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Frequency Capping; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: geo_targeting
attributes.description: Geographic targeting parameters applied to this trafficking instruction, specifying the countries, regions, DMAs, or cities where the ad should be served. Expressed as a structured targeting string or comma-separated location codes.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Geo Targeting; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: impression_tracking_pixel_url
attributes.description: URL of the impression tracking pixel fired upon each ad impression to record delivery counts. Used for third-party verification, billing reconciliation, and campaign measurement. May include multiple pixels concatenated or the primary pixel URL.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Impression Tracking; MRC Digital Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: instruction_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable reference number for this trafficking instruction, used in communications with ad servers, media vendors, and internal trafficking teams. Typically follows a structured naming convention (e.g., TI-2024-00123).
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: instruction_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the trafficking instruction: pending (created but not yet dispatched), sent (transmitted to ad server or vendor), confirmed (acknowledged by recipient), rejected (refused by recipient), or cancelled (voided before confirmation).
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Workflow; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: instruction_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the trafficking instruction: new (initial dispatch of a creative), revision (update to an existing instruction), cancellation (termination of delivery), pause (temporary halt), or resume (restart after pause).
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Workflow; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special instructions, or contextual information relevant to this trafficking instruction. Used by ad operations teams to communicate nuances not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking; Workfront - Project Notes

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason provided by the ad server or media vendor when a trafficking instruction is rejected. Populated only when instruction_status is 'rejected'. Used for troubleshooting and resubmission workflows.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Error Handling; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this trafficking instruction, incremented each time a revision instruction is issued for the same placement and creative combination. Version 1 represents the original instruction.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Versioning; Workfront - Change Management

attributes.name: sent_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the trafficking instruction was transmitted to the ad server or media vendor. Used for SLA tracking, audit trails, and delivery timeline analysis.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking Audit; IAB Digital Advertising Guidelines

attributes.name: third_party_verification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether third-party ad verification (e.g., DoubleVerify, Integral Ad Science) is mandated for this trafficking instruction per client or campaign requirements. When true, verification tags must be included in the ad serving setup.
attributes.references: TAG Certified Against Fraud; MRC Accreditation Standards; IAB Quality Assurance Guidelines

attributes.name: trafficking_date
attributes.description: The date on which the trafficking instruction was formally issued and dispatched to the ad server or media vendor. Represents the principal real-world business event date for this operational record.
attributes.references: Google Campaign Manager 360 - Ad Trafficking; Mediaocean Prisma - Trafficking Workflow

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this trafficking instruction record was last modified. Tracks revisions to the instruction for audit, compliance, and change management purposes.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity; IAB Data Governance Guidelines

attributes.name: vast_tag_url
attributes.business_glossary_term: Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) Tag URL
attributes.description: The Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) tag URL used for video creative delivery. Provides the ad server with the XML-based instructions for serving video ads, including media file location, tracking events, and companion ads. Applicable for video placements.
attributes.references: IAB VAST Standard (Video Ad Serving Template); Google Campaign Manager 360 - Video Trafficking

attributes.name: viewability_tag_url
attributes.description: URL of the viewability measurement tag embedded in the ad creative to track whether the ad was viewable per MRC and IAB viewability standards (e.g., 50% of pixels in view for 1 continuous second for display). Used for viewability reporting and vendor compliance.
attributes.references: MRC Viewability Standards; IAB Viewability Guidelines; Google Campaign Manager 360 - Viewability Measurement

attributes.name: vpaid_tag_url
attributes.business_glossary_term: Video Player-Ad Interface Definition (VPAID) Tag URL
attributes.description: The Video Player-Ad Interface Definition (VPAID) tag URL enabling interactive video ad execution within the video player environment. Used for rich interactive video creatives requiring player-level communication. Applicable for VPAID-enabled placements.
attributes.references: IAB VPAID Standard (Video Player-Ad Interface Definition); Google Campaign Manager 360 - Video Trafficking

products.name: sov_benchmark
products.description: Reference master capturing Share of Voice (SOV) benchmarks and competitive media spending intelligence used during media planning to set investment levels and justify budget recommendations. Captures brand/advertiser, competitor set, channel type, market/DMA, measurement period, SOV percentage, estimated competitor spend, total category spend, data source (Nielsen Ad Intel, Comscore, Pathmatics/Sensor Tower), benchmark date, and confidence level. Owned by media domain because SOV benchmarks directly drive media budget allocation decisions and are consumed primarily by media strategists during the planning phase. Distinct from brand health metrics (brand domain) in that this measures media investment share, not brand perception.
products.reference: SOV (Share of Voice) — Nielsen Ad Intel / Comscore

attributes.name: sov_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Share of Voice (SOV) benchmark record in the media planning reference master.

attributes.name: ad_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to media.ad_channel. Business justification: sov_benchmark currently has channel_type as a STRING attribute. SOV benchmarks capture Share of Voice and competitive media spending intelligence for specific advertising channels (e.g., SOV in Displa

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertiser or brand whose SOV position is being benchmarked. Links to the advertiser master in the client domain.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.segment. Business justification: Share-of-voice benchmarks are measured and reported against specific audience segments for competitive analysis. Planners use segment-level SOV data to inform budget allocation and channel strategy de

attributes.name: brand_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to brand.brand_profile. Business justification: SOV benchmarks measure brand performance against competitive set. Brand profile provides SOV tracking configuration, competitive set definition, and target SOV percentages. Core to SOV reporting, comp

attributes.name: benchmark_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this SOV benchmark record, used for cross-system referencing in Nielsen Ad Intel, Comscore, and Mediaocean Prisma.
attributes.references: IAB Data Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: benchmark_date
attributes.description: The date on which this SOV benchmark record was captured or published. Represents the as-of date for the competitive intelligence snapshot, distinct from the measurement period dates.
attributes.references: MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: benchmark_name
attributes.description: Human-readable label for this benchmark record, typically describing the brand, channel, and measurement period (e.g., 'Acme Brand — Paid Search — Q1 2024 — National').

attributes.name: benchmark_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this SOV benchmark record. Active = current reference used in planning; Superseded = replaced by a newer benchmark; Draft = pending validation; Archived = historical record; Under Review = flagged for data quality review.
attributes.references: IAB Data Standards; MRC Data Quality Guidelines

attributes.name: competitor_names
attributes.description: Comma-delimited list of individual competitor brand names included in the defined competitor set for this SOV benchmark. Confidential competitive intelligence sourced from Nielsen Ad Intel or Pathmatics.

attributes.name: competitor_set_name
attributes.description: Label identifying the defined group of competing brands or advertisers included in the SOV calculation (e.g., 'Tier-1 Auto Competitors — Luxury Segment'). Confidential competitive intelligence.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative confidence rating for the accuracy of the SOV and spend estimates in this benchmark record. Reflects data source quality, sample size, and methodology robustness. High = MRC-accredited source with full panel; Indicative = modeled or extrapolated estimate.
attributes.references: MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: confidence_score
attributes.description: Numeric confidence score (0.00–100.00) quantifying the statistical reliability of the SOV benchmark estimate. Complements the qualitative confidence_level field with a precise measure for analytics and model inputs.
attributes.references: MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the country in which the SOV benchmark is measured (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this SOV benchmark record was first created in the system. Audit trail field conforming to the yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: The primary data source or platform from which the SOV and competitive spend data was obtained. Drives confidence assessment and methodology notes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nielsen_ad_intel|comscore|pathmatics|sensor_tower|kantar|mediaocean_prisma|internal_estimate|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: MRC Accreditation Standards; Nielsen Ad Intel; Comscore Methodology

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned three-digit numeric code for the Designated Market Area (DMA) associated with this SOV benchmark. Use '000' for national/non-DMA benchmarks.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Code Registry; MRC Geographic Standards

attributes.name: estimated_brand_spend
attributes.description: Estimated total media spend (in USD) for the advertiser's brand within the defined channel, market, and measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Ad Intel, Comscore, or Pathmatics/Sensor Tower competitive intelligence.
attributes.references: Nielsen Ad Intel Methodology; Comscore Ad Metrix; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: estimated_competitor_spend
attributes.description: Estimated total media spend (in USD) for all competitors in the defined competitor set within the channel, market, and measurement period. Sourced from competitive intelligence platforms.
attributes.references: Nielsen Ad Intel Methodology; Comscore Ad Metrix; 4As Competitive Intelligence Guidelines

attributes.name: grp_benchmark
attributes.description: The Gross Rating Point (GRP) benchmark value for the advertiser's brand within the defined channel, market, and measurement period. Used for broadcast and video channel SOV benchmarking alongside spend-based SOV.
attributes.references: MRC GRP Measurement Standards; Nielsen GRP Methodology; IAB

attributes.name: impression_share_pct
attributes.description: The advertiser's share of total available impressions within the defined channel, market, and measurement period. Particularly relevant for digital channels (paid search, display) as a complement to spend-based SOV.
attributes.references: IAB Impression Measurement Guidelines; MRC Digital Measurement Standards; Google Campaign Manager 360

attributes.name: is_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SOV benchmark record has been validated and approved by a media strategist or analytics team member before use in client-facing media planning recommendations.
attributes.references: MRC Data Quality Guidelines; 4As Quality Assurance Standards

attributes.name: market_name
attributes.description: Name of the geographic market or Nielsen Designated Market Area (DMA) for which the SOV benchmark applies (e.g., 'New York DMA', 'National', 'Los Angeles DMA').
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; MRC Geographic Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_type
attributes.description: Granularity of the measurement period for this SOV benchmark (e.g., weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual, or custom date range).
attributes.references: MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: methodology_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of the measurement methodology, data collection approach, or estimation technique used to derive the SOV and spend figures. Captures caveats, panel definitions, or extrapolation methods for transparency.
attributes.references: MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Measurement Standards

attributes.name: period_end_date
attributes.description: Last date of the measurement period covered by this SOV benchmark record. Together with period_start_date defines the competitive intelligence window.

attributes.name: period_start_date
attributes.description: First date of the measurement period covered by this SOV benchmark record. Used to align competitive spend intelligence with media planning cycles.

attributes.name: planning_cycle
attributes.description: The media planning cycle or fiscal period for which this benchmark is intended to inform investment decisions (e.g., 'FY2024', 'Q2 2024', 'H1 2024'). Links the benchmark to the relevant planning horizon.
attributes.references: 4As Media Planning Standards; ANA Media Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: product_category
attributes.description: The IAB or Nielsen-defined product or service category within which the SOV benchmark is measured (e.g., 'Automotive — Luxury Vehicles', 'Quick Service Restaurants'). Defines the competitive universe.
attributes.references: IAB Content Taxonomy; Nielsen Product Category Definitions

attributes.name: recommended_budget
attributes.description: The media budget (in spend_currency_code) recommended by media strategists to achieve the sov_target_pct for the advertiser's brand in the defined channel and market. Derived from competitive intelligence and used in client budget justification.
attributes.references: 4As Media Planning Standards; ANA Media Planning Guidelines; Mediaocean Prisma

attributes.name: sov_pct
attributes.description: The measured or estimated Share of Voice (SOV) percentage for the advertiser's brand within the defined competitor set, channel, and market for the measurement period. Expressed as a percentage (0.0000–100.0000). Core metric driving media budget allocation recommendations.
attributes.references: IAB SOV Measurement Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; ANA

attributes.name: sov_target_pct
attributes.description: The planned or recommended SOV percentage target set by media strategists for the advertiser's brand during the planning phase. Used to justify budget recommendations and measure gap versus current SOV.
attributes.references: IAB SOV Measurement Standards; ANA Media Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: spend_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all spend figures in this benchmark record (estimated_brand_spend, estimated_competitor_spend, total_category_spend). Defaults to USD for US markets.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: total_category_spend
attributes.description: Estimated total media spend (in USD) across all advertisers in the product/service category within the channel, market, and measurement period. Denominator used to calculate SOV percentage.
attributes.references: Nielsen Ad Intel Methodology; Comscore Ad Metrix; IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: trp_benchmark
attributes.description: The Target Rating Point (TRP) benchmark value for the advertiser's brand, scoped to the defined target audience segment. Complements GRP by focusing on the specific audience rather than the total population.
attributes.references: MRC TRP Measurement Standards; Nielsen TRP Methodology; IAB

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this SOV benchmark record was last modified. Supports data lineage tracking and audit compliance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); IAB Data Standards

attributes.name: verified_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the media strategist or analytics team member who validated and approved this SOV benchmark record for use in planning.
attributes.references: 4As Quality Assurance Standards; MRC Data Quality Guidelines

attributes.name: verified_date
attributes.description: Date on which this SOV benchmark record was verified and approved by the responsible media strategist or analytics team member.
attributes.references: 4As Quality Assurance Standards; MRC Data Quality Guidelines

products.name: audience_rating
products.description: Reference data capturing third-party audience measurement ratings for media vehicles — including Nielsen TV ratings, Comscore digital audience data, and radio ratings. Captures vehicle name (network, station, site), daypart/time slot, demographic cell (age/gender), rating value, universe estimate, average audience, cumulative audience, measurement period, measurement source (Nielsen, Comscore, MRC-accredited), and data vintage. Used to validate GRP/TRP delivery and inform media planning decisions.
products.reference: Audience Ratings — Nielsen Ad Intel / Comscore / MRC

attributes.name: audience_rating_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each audience rating record in the media vehicle measurement dataset. Primary key for the audience_rating data product.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.segment. Business justification: Audience ratings measure delivery against specific demographic and behavioral segments for GRP/TRP calculation. Buyers use segment-linked ratings for media planning, buying, and post-campaign delivery

attributes.name: publisher_id
attributes.description: Reference to the publisher or media owner associated with this rated vehicle. Used to aggregate ratings across a publisher's portfolio.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Publisher Standards; Comscore Media Metrix

attributes.name: publisher_property_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media vehicle (network, station, site, or publication) for which this audience rating applies. Links to the media vehicle master record.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Media Taxonomy; Nielsen Station Index

attributes.name: age_range_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the age range for the demographic cell (e.g., 49 for the A18-49 cell). A null value indicates an open-ended upper bound (e.g., '65+').
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement; Comscore Unified Digital Measurement

attributes.name: age_range_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the age range for the demographic cell (e.g., 18 for the A18-49 cell). Enables precise demographic filtering and TRP validation in media planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement; Comscore Unified Digital Measurement

attributes.name: average_audience
attributes.description: Average number of persons (in thousands) tuned to or engaged with the media vehicle during the average minute of the measured time slot. The primary audience delivery metric used in GRP/TRP calculations and media plan validation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Average Audience Methodology; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: confidence_interval
attributes.description: Statistical confidence interval (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.95 for 95%) associated with the rating estimate, reflecting measurement precision. Used by media planners to assess reliability of ratings for planning and reconciliation decisions.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Statistical Methodology; Comscore Measurement Accuracy Standards

attributes.name: cumulative_audience
attributes.description: Total unduplicated number of persons (in thousands) who were exposed to the media vehicle at least once during the measurement period. Also known as 'reach' or 'cume'. Used in reach and frequency planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Cume Audience Methodology; Comscore Reach Measurement; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: currency_type
attributes.description: The audience measurement currency in which this rating is expressed (e.g., 'grp' for Gross Rating Points, 'trp' for Target Rating Points, 'impressions' for digital impression-based measurement). Aligns with IAB and MRC currency standards for cross-media planning.
attributes.references: IAB Cross-Media Audience Measurement Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; Nielsen One Currency

attributes.name: data_vintage_date
attributes.description: The date on which this specific version of the rating data was published or released by the measurement source. Enables tracking of data revisions and ensures media planners are using the most current ratings vintage for planning and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Data Release Calendar; Comscore Data Vintage Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: daypart_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the daypart or time slot for which the rating is measured (e.g., 'PRIME', 'EARLY_NEWS', 'LATE_FRINGE', 'MORNING_DRIVE'). Aligns with Nielsen and MRC daypart definitions used in media planning and GRP/TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Daypart Definitions; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; IAB Video Ad Spend Report

attributes.name: daypart_name
attributes.description: Human-readable label for the daypart or time slot (e.g., 'Prime Time', 'Early Morning', 'Late Night'). Used in media planning reports and client-facing deliverables.
attributes.references: Nielsen Daypart Definitions; Mediaocean Prisma Media Planning Standards

attributes.name: gender_segment
attributes.description: Gender component of the demographic cell for which the rating is reported. 'persons' and 'all' indicate total audience regardless of gender, consistent with Nielsen P2+ and Comscore total audience reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement Demographic Standards; Comscore Unified Digital Measurement; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: geography_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific geographic market for this rating (e.g., Nielsen DMA code '501' for New York, MSA FIPS code, or 'US' for national). Used to match ratings to media plan geographic targets.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Code List; US Census FIPS Codes; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: geography_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the geographic market for this rating (e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'National'). Used in media planning reports and client-facing deliverables.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Market Definitions; Comscore Geographic Reporting

attributes.name: geography_type
attributes.description: The geographic scope of the audience measurement (e.g., 'national' for national ratings, 'dma' for Nielsen Designated Market Area, 'msa' for Metropolitan Statistical Area). Determines the applicable universe estimate and planning geography.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; MRC Geographic Measurement Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: grp_contribution
attributes.description: The Gross Rating Point (GRP) value contributed by a single exposure on this vehicle in this daypart for the total audience demographic. GRP = Rating × Number of Spots. Stored at the unit level to support media plan GRP accumulation and delivery validation.
attributes.references: IAB GRP Standards; Nielsen GRP Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: ingested_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audience rating record was first ingested into the Databricks Silver Layer from the source measurement system (Nielsen Ad Intel or Comscore). Supports data lineage and audit trail for the lakehouse pipeline.
attributes.references: MRC Data Provenance Requirements; IAB Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: is_low_reliability
attributes.description: Flag indicating that this rating record has been identified as statistically unreliable due to insufficient sample size, high margin of error, or measurement source quality flags. Low-reliability ratings should not be used for billing reconciliation without additional validation.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Data Quality Flags; Comscore Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: measurement_methodology
attributes.description: The data collection methodology used by the measurement source to produce this rating (e.g., 'panel' for Nielsen People Meter, 'census' for Comscore digital census tags, 'hybrid' for blended panel+census). Affects data quality and comparability across sources.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; Comscore Unified Digital Measurement

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the audience measurement sweep or reporting period during which this rating was collected. Together with measurement_period_start, defines the temporal scope of the rating data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Sweeps Calendar; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; Mediaocean Prisma Reconciliation Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the audience measurement sweep or reporting period during which this rating was collected (e.g., Nielsen sweeps period start). Used to align ratings data with campaign flight dates for GRP/TRP delivery validation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Sweeps Calendar; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; Mediaocean Prisma Reconciliation Standards

attributes.name: measurement_source
attributes.description: The third-party audience measurement provider that produced this rating data (e.g., 'nielsen', 'comscore'). Determines the methodology, panel, and accreditation status applicable to this record. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nielsen|comscore|arbitron|mri_simmons|kantar|doubleclick — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: MRC Accreditation Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; TAG Certified Measurement

attributes.name: mrc_accredited
attributes.description: Indicates whether the measurement source and methodology for this rating record hold current Media Rating Council (MRC) accreditation. MRC-accredited data is the industry standard for media buying and billing reconciliation.
attributes.references: MRC Accreditation Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: The delivery platform for which this audience rating applies (e.g., 'linear_tv', 'streaming', 'digital_video', 'audio'). Supports cross-platform audience deduplication and unified reach planning across CTV/OTT, linear, and digital channels. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_tv|streaming|digital_display|digital_video|audio|print|ooh|dooh — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Cross-Media Audience Measurement Standards; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement; Comscore Cross-Platform Reporting

attributes.name: rating_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of the rating record indicating whether the data is preliminary (initial estimate), final (confirmed), revised (updated after initial release), or superseded (replaced by a newer vintage). Critical for media reconciliation — only 'final' ratings are used for billing reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Data Release Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines; Mediaocean Prisma Reconciliation

attributes.name: rating_value
attributes.description: The audience rating expressed as a percentage of the total universe that viewed/listened to/visited the media vehicle during the measured time slot and demographic cell. A rating of 5.25 means 5.25% of the universe was exposed. Core metric for GRP and TRP delivery validation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of panel respondents or measurement units contributing to this rating estimate. Smaller sample sizes indicate lower statistical reliability; used to apply confidence intervals and flag low-reliability ratings in media planning.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Sample Size Reporting; Comscore Methodology Documentation

attributes.name: share_value
attributes.description: Percentage of the Households Using Television (HUT) or Persons Using Television (PUT) that were tuned to this vehicle during the time slot. Share = (Average Audience / HUT or PUT) × 100. Used alongside rating to assess competitive performance.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Share Methodology; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: time_slot_end
attributes.description: End time of the measured time slot in HH:MM (24-hour) format (e.g., '23:00' for 11 PM). Defines the close of the measurement window.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: time_slot_start
attributes.description: Start time of the measured time slot in HH:MM (24-hour) format (e.g., '20:00' for 8 PM). Used to precisely define the measurement window within a daypart.
attributes.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: trp_contribution
attributes.description: The Target Rating Point (TRP) value contributed by a single exposure on this vehicle for the specific demographic cell. TRP = Target Demographic Rating × Number of Spots. Used to validate targeted audience delivery against media plan objectives.
attributes.references: IAB TRP Standards; Nielsen TRP Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: universe_estimate
attributes.description: Total estimated population size (in persons) for the demographic cell and geography against which the rating is calculated. Used as the denominator in rating calculations and for projecting absolute audience size from rating percentages.
attributes.references: Nielsen Universe Estimates; Comscore Unified Digital Measurement; MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this audience rating record, including revisions from the measurement source or corrections applied during reconciliation. Used to track data freshness and identify revised ratings vintages.
attributes.references: MRC Data Provenance Requirements; IAB Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: vehicle_type
attributes.description: Classification of the media vehicle by channel type. Determines which measurement methodology and rating currency applies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: broadcast_tv|cable_tv|radio|digital|print|ooh|ctv_ott|podcast — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Media Taxonomy; MRC Cross-Media Audience Measurement Standards

products.name: ad_channel
products.description: Master reference entity for all media and distribution channels through which advertising is delivered — including paid search (SEM/PPC), social, display, video, email, SEO, OOH/DOOH, CTV/OTT, and programmatic. Owns the authoritative channel taxonomy with IAB-aligned classifications, channel codes, and delivery modalities. Also owns platform-specific operational configuration including DSP seat settings (The Trade Desk), UTM parameter conventions, bid strategy defaults, frequency cap policies, brand safety keyword lists, and GDPR/CCPA consent signal handling. SSOT for channel identity, taxonomy, and operational configuration across the enterprise.

attributes.name: ad_channel_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the advertising channel. Primary key for the ad_channel entity.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to media.category. Business justification: ad_channel currently has channel_category as a STRING attribute. The category product exists to provide hierarchical classification taxonomy for advertising channels. This FK normalizes the channel-to

attributes.name: agency_commission_pct
attributes.description: Standard agency commission percentage applied to gross media spend on this channel. Typically 15% for traditional media, 10-15% for digital. Null if commission varies by client or IO.

attributes.name: api_endpoint_url
attributes.description: Base URL for the channels API integration. Used by ETL processes to retrieve campaign performance data, update bids, and sync creative assets. Confidential system configuration.

attributes.name: api_version
attributes.description: Version of the API specification currently in use for this channel (e.g., v14, 2023-Q4). Critical for maintaining integration compatibility during platform upgrades.

attributes.name: attribution_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days after an ad interaction (click or view) during which conversions are attributed to this channel. Standard windows are 1, 7, 30, or 90 days depending on channel and business model.

attributes.name: bid_strategy_default
attributes.description: Default bidding strategy applied to campaigns on this channel unless overridden at campaign level. Determines how the platform optimizes bids to achieve campaign objectives. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: manual_cpc|enhanced_cpc|maximize_clicks|maximize_conversions|target_cpa|target_roas|target_impression_share|viewable_cpm — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: brand_safety_keywords
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of keywords or content categories to exclude for brand safety (e.g., violence, adult content, controversial topics). Applied as negative targeting across all campaigns on this channel.

attributes.name: brand_safety_tier
attributes.description: Default brand safety filtering level applied to inventory on this channel. Standard allows broad reach; strict applies maximum content exclusions to protect brand reputation.

attributes.name: ccpa_opt_out_supported
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Opt-Out Supported
attributes.description: Indicates whether this channel supports CCPA Do Not Sell signals for California users. Required for compliance with California privacy regulations.

attributes.name: channel_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the channel across all systems (e.g., SEM_GOOGLE, SOCIAL_FB, DISPLAY_PROG). Used as the business identifier in campaign planning, trafficking, and reporting.

attributes.name: channel_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the advertising channel (e.g., Google Search, Facebook Social, Programmatic Display).

attributes.name: channel_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the channel. Active channels are available for campaign planning and buying; deprecated channels are phased out but may have historical data.

attributes.name: channel_type
attributes.description: Primary classification of the channel by media type. Aligns with IAB taxonomy for cross-platform reporting and planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paid_search|social|display|video|email|seo|ooh|dooh|ctv|ott|programmatic|audio|native|affiliate — 14 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: click_attribution_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days after a click during which conversions are attributed to this channel. Typically longer than view attribution window due to higher intent signal.

attributes.name: consent_signal_format
attributes.description: Format of privacy consent signals passed to this channel. TCF v2 (Transparency and Consent Framework) for GDPR, US Privacy String for CCPA, GPP (Global Privacy Platform) for multi-jurisdiction compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this channel record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Default currency for financial transactions on this channel. Three-letter ISO 4217 code (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Used for rate cards, billing, and reconciliation.

attributes.name: delivery_modality
attributes.description: Method by which media is bought and delivered through this channel. Determines operational workflow, trafficking requirements, and reconciliation processes.

attributes.name: dsp_seat_code
attributes.description: Unique seat identifier within the DSP platform (e.g., The Trade Desk seat ID). Used for programmatic bid requests, deal configuration, and reconciliation. Confidential operational credential.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this channel configuration became active and available for campaign planning and buying. Used for historical tracking of channel availability.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this channel configuration expires or was deprecated. Null for active channels. Used to track channel lifecycle and prevent planning on sunset channels.

attributes.name: frequency_cap_default
attributes.description: Default maximum number of times an ad can be shown to the same user within the frequency cap period. Prevents ad fatigue and optimizes reach. Null indicates no default cap.

attributes.name: frequency_cap_period_default
attributes.description: Time window over which the default frequency cap is applied (e.g., 3 impressions per day). Works in conjunction with frequency_cap_default.

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Consent Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether GDPR consent signals must be passed for users in EU/EEA jurisdictions when serving ads on this channel. True for channels operating in or targeting European markets.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or configuration details specific to this channel. Used by media planners and buyers for reference.

attributes.name: platform_name
attributes.description: Name of the technology platform or publisher that operates this channel (e.g., Google Ads, Meta Business Suite, The Trade Desk, Hulu).

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: Classification of the underlying technology platform. DSP (Demand-Side Platform) for programmatic buying, SSP (Supply-Side Platform) for inventory supply, or direct publisher platforms. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dsp|ssp|ad_network|publisher_direct|search_engine|social_platform|video_platform|email_platform|ad_server — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: pricing_model
attributes.description: Default pricing model for media buys on this channel. CPM (Cost Per Mille) for impressions, CPC (Cost Per Click), CPA (Cost Per Acquisition), CPV (Cost Per View), CPCV (Cost Per Completed View), or flat fee. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cpm|cpc|cpa|cpv|cpcv|flat_fee|performance — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: supports_audience_targeting
attributes.description: Indicates whether this channel supports audience segment targeting using first-party, third-party, or platform-native audience data. Critical for personalized campaign strategies.

attributes.name: supports_dayparting
attributes.description: Indicates whether this channel supports daypart scheduling (time-of-day and day-of-week targeting). Common in broadcast, CTV, and digital channels for optimizing reach and frequency.

attributes.name: supports_geo_targeting
attributes.description: Indicates whether this channel supports geographic targeting by country, region, DMA (Designated Market Area), postal code, or radius. Essential for local and regional campaigns.

attributes.name: supports_programmatic
attributes.description: Indicates whether this channel supports programmatic buying via DSP platforms and RTB (Real-Time Bidding) protocols. True for most digital channels; false for traditional media.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this channel record was last modified. Used for change tracking, cache invalidation, and audit purposes.

attributes.name: utm_medium_default
attributes.description: Default value for utm_medium parameter in campaign tracking URLs for this channel (e.g., cpc, social, display). Enables consistent channel attribution in web analytics.

attributes.name: utm_source_default
attributes.description: Default value for utm_source parameter in campaign tracking URLs for this channel. Standardizes attribution and analytics reporting across Google Analytics and other web analytics platforms.

attributes.name: view_attribution_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days after an ad view (impression without click) during which conversions are attributed to this channel. Typically 1-7 days for display and video channels.

attributes.name: viewability_standard
attributes.description: Viewability measurement standard applied to this channel. MRC (Media Rating Council) standard requires 50% of pixels in view for 1 second (display) or 2 seconds (video).

attributes.name: viewability_threshold_pct
attributes.description: Minimum viewability percentage required for impressions on this channel to be considered valid for billing and reporting purposes. Typically 50-70% based on MRC standards.

products.name: category
products.description: Hierarchical classification taxonomy for advertising channels — defining top-level channel families (e.g., Digital, Broadcast, Print, OOH), sub-categories (e.g., Programmatic Display, Paid Social, CTV/OTT), and leaf-level channel types. Supports IAB and MRC-aligned channel categorization used in media planning, reporting, and billing reconciliation.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the advertising channel category. Primary key for the category taxonomy.

attributes.name: parent_category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent category in the hierarchical taxonomy. Null for top-level channel families.

attributes.name: ad_format_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ad formats supported by this category (e.g., banner, video, native, audio, interstitial, rich media). Used for creative trafficking and asset management.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Ad Format Guidelines

attributes.name: audience_targeting_capability
attributes.description: Level of audience segmentation and targeting available for this category. Advanced = behavioral, contextual, lookalike; basic = demographic + interest; demographic_only = age/gender only; none = broad reach only.

attributes.name: brand_safety_tier
attributes.description: Default brand safety classification for inventory within this category. Premium = curated, brand-safe publishers; standard = verified inventory; open_exchange = programmatic open marketplace; unverified = requires additional screening.

attributes.name: buying_method
attributes.description: Primary buying approach associated with this category (e.g., direct IO, programmatic RTB, upfront commitment, scatter market). Guides procurement workflow and system routing.

attributes.name: category_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier code for the category used in media planning and reporting systems. Follows IAB-aligned naming conventions.

attributes.name: category_description
attributes.description: Detailed business definition and usage guidance for this category. Includes scope, examples, and differentiation from related categories. Used for planner training and taxonomy governance.

attributes.name: category_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the advertising channel category (e.g., Digital Display, Programmatic Video, Paid Social, Broadcast TV, Out-of-Home).

attributes.name: category_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the category. Active categories are available for media planning and buying; deprecated categories are retained for historical reporting only.

attributes.name: category_type
attributes.description: Classification level within the taxonomy hierarchy: channel_family (top-level such as Digital, Broadcast, Print, OOH), channel_subcategory (mid-level such as Programmatic Display, Paid Social), or channel_type (leaf-level granular channel).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this category record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and taxonomy change tracking.

attributes.name: daypart_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether daypart scheduling (time-of-day targeting such as prime time, daytime, late night) is relevant for this category. Primarily applicable to broadcast, radio, and linear TV.

attributes.name: default_attribution_window_days
attributes.description: Standard attribution lookback window (in days) for conversion tracking in this category. Used for ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) and CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) measurement.

attributes.name: default_pricing_model
attributes.description: Standard pricing model typically used for this category: CPM (Cost Per Mille), CPC (Cost Per Click), CPA (Cost Per Acquisition), CPV (Cost Per View), flat fee, daypart rate, or GRP-based pricing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cpm|cpc|cpa|cpv|flat_fee|daypart|grp — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this category was deprecated or retired. Null for currently active categories. Supports historical reporting and taxonomy evolution tracking.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this category became active and available for use in media planning and buying. Supports temporal taxonomy versioning.

attributes.name: frequency_cap_support
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category supports frequency capping (limiting the number of times a user sees an ad within a time period). Common in digital and CTV/OTT channels.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Frequency Management Guidelines

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Typical geographic reach classification for this category. DMA = Designated Market Area (Nielsen standard for US broadcast markets).

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of this category in the taxonomy tree. Level 1 = top-level channel family, Level 2 = subcategory, Level 3+ = leaf-level types.

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Full hierarchical path from root to this category, represented as a delimited string (e.g., Digital > Programmatic > Display). Used for rollup reporting and navigation.

attributes.name: iab_category_code
attributes.description: Official IAB Tech Lab category code mapping for this channel category. Ensures interoperability with IAB-compliant ad servers, DSPs, and SSPs.

attributes.name: is_addressable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category supports addressable (audience-targeted, household-level) advertising capabilities, common in CTV (Connected TV), OTT (Over-the-Top), and digital channels.

attributes.name: is_leaf_node
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category is a terminal leaf node (true) or a parent node with children (false). Leaf nodes are used for actual media placement assignment.

attributes.name: is_programmatic
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category represents programmatic (automated, Real-Time Bidding) media buying channels. Used to route placements to DSP (Demand-Side Platform) and SSP (Supply-Side Platform) systems.

attributes.name: measurement_standard
attributes.description: Industry measurement standard or methodology applicable to this category (e.g., Nielsen GRP, Comscore vCE, MOAT Viewability, IAS Brand Safety). Used for performance tracking and reconciliation.

attributes.name: media_type
attributes.description: High-level media classification for this category. Aligns with industry-standard media type groupings used in media planning, buying, and MRC (Media Rating Council) reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: digital|broadcast|print|ooh|audio|ctv_ott|social|search|native|email — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: mrc_accredited
attributes.description: Indicates whether measurement for this category is covered by MRC-accredited methodologies. Critical for advertiser trust and audit compliance.

attributes.name: reconciliation_method
attributes.description: Standard billing reconciliation approach for this category. Automated = system-to-system delivery log matching; manual = invoice-based reconciliation; hybrid = combination; not_applicable = non-billable category.

attributes.name: requires_trafficking
attributes.description: Indicates whether placements in this category require formal ad trafficking instructions (creative asset delivery, tag generation, third-party verification setup) via ad servers such as Google Campaign Manager 360.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Ad Operations Guidelines

attributes.name: sort_order
attributes.description: Display sequence number for this category within its parent level. Used for consistent ordering in media planning UI, reports, and dashboards.

attributes.name: supports_grp
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category supports GRP-based planning and measurement, typically applicable to broadcast and linear TV channels.

attributes.name: supports_trp
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category supports TRP-based audience targeting and measurement, used for demographic-specific reach planning.

attributes.name: supports_viewability
attributes.description: Indicates whether this category supports MRC-compliant viewability measurement (e.g., 50% of pixels in-view for 1+ seconds for display, 2+ seconds for video).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this category record. Used for change detection and incremental processing in downstream analytics.

attributes.name: usage_notes
attributes.description: Operational notes and best practices for using this category in media planning, buying, and reporting. May include system-specific routing instructions or billing considerations.

attributes.name: vast_vpaid_support
attributes.business_glossary_term: VAST (Video Ad Serving Template) / VPAID (Video Player-Ad Interface Definition) Support
attributes.description: Indicates video ad serving standard support for this category. VAST for linear video ads, VPAID for interactive video ads, both for hybrid support, none for non-video categories.

products.name: publisher_property
products.description: Represents individual media properties, sites, apps, networks, or placements owned or operated by a publisher — e.g., a specific website, mobile app, TV network, OOH billboard network, or streaming channel. Captures property-level attributes including URL/app ID, content vertical, audience composition, MRC-audited traffic certification, viewability benchmarks, and brand safety classification.

attributes.name: publisher_property_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the publisher property. Primary key.

attributes.name: publisher_id
attributes.description: Reference to the publisher or media owner that operates this property.

attributes.name: ad_fraud_risk_score

products.description: Master record representing the client-facing media flowchart — the primary planning deliverable produced by media planners showing the visual/tabular allocation of media spend across channels, vehicles, markets, and flight periods. products.name: channel_supplier_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the commercial agreement between an advertising channel and a supplier (media publisher or technology platform). It captures channel-specific supplier relationships including preferred vendor status, negotiated commission rates, spend commitments, and service level agreements. Each record links one ad_channel to one supplier with attributes that exist only in the context of this channel-supplier partnership. This is the operational SSOT for media buying teams to understand which suppliers are approved and preferred for each channel, and what commercial terms apply.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, suppliers (publishers and tech platforms) provide inventory and services across multiple advertising channels (Google Search, Facebook Social, programmatic display, CTV, etc.), and each channel sources from multiple suppliers. Agencies negotiate channel-specific commercial agreements with suppliers that include unique commission rates, spend commitments, preferred vendor status, and SLA terms that vary by channel-supplier combination. Media buying teams actively manage these relationships to determine which suppliers are approved for each channel and what commercial terms apply.

products.name: format_availability
products.description: This association product represents the availability and commercial terms of specific ad formats offered by publishers. It captures format-specific inventory availability, pricing, performance metrics, and brand safety attributes that exist only in the context of a publisher-format combination. Each record links one ad_format to one publisher with commercial and operational attributes managed by media planning and buying teams.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, publishers offer multiple ad formats (display, video, native, audio, DOOH) and each format is available from multiple publishers. Media planners actively manage format availability across publishers, tracking format-specific pricing (floor CPM, average CPM), inventory volume (monthly impressions), and performance metrics (viewability rate, brand safety tier) that exist only at the publisher-format combination level. Rate cards, availability forecasts, and programmatic deals are negotiated and tracked per publisher-format pair.

products.name: io_creative_trafficking
products.description: This association product represents the operational trafficking relationship between media insertion orders and creative assets. It captures the assignment of specific creative assets to specific IOs for execution, including flight dates, rotation weights, trafficking status, and approval workflows. Each record links one IO to one creative asset with attributes that exist only in the context of this trafficking assignment.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, a single IO routinely executes with multiple creative assets simultaneously (A/B testing, format variations for display/video/mobile, sequential messaging strategies, dayparting rotations). Conversely, a single creative asset is frequently trafficked across multiple IOs when campaigns span multiple publishers, extended flight periods requiring separate IOs, or when the same creative is reused across different advertiser campaigns. The trafficking relationship itself is an operational business process managed by media traffickers.

products.name: allocation
products.description: This association product represents the allocation relationship between media_plan and work_package. It captures the distribution of project work effort and budget across media execution artifacts. Each record links one media_plan to one work_package with attributes that track how project resources (time, cost, budget) are allocated to specific media planning and buying deliverables, enabling cross-charging, billing attribution, and effort tracking across the project-to-media boundary.. Existence Justification: In advertising agency operations, media plans and work packages represent different organizational views of the same work: media plans organize by client deliverable and media execution artifact, while work packages organize by project structure and resource allocation. A single media plan (e.g., Q1 Digital Campaign for Client X) typically requires effort from multiple work packages (Media Planning, Media Buying, Trafficking, Optimization), and a single work package (e.g., Media Buying Q1) typically supports multiple client media plans simultaneously. The allocation relationship tracks how project resources (effort hours, costs) are distributed across media execution artifacts for billing attribution, cost tracking, and resource utilization analysis.

products.name: plan_asset_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the planned assignment of creative assets to media plans during the media planning phase. It captures which creative assets are planned for use in which media plans, including planned usage timing, rotation weighting, channel-specific assignments, market-specific assignments, and trafficking priority. Each record links one media plan to one creative asset with attributes that exist only in the context of this planned usage relationship.. Existence Justification: In advertising operations, media plans routinely use multiple creative assets to support different channels, markets, formats, and rotation strategies within a single plan. Conversely, creative assets—especially evergreen brand assets, seasonal campaign assets, and multi-market assets—are reused across multiple media plans over time. The business actively manages these assignments during the media planning phase, tracking planned usage dates, rotation weights, channel/market assignments, and trafficking priorities for each plan-asset pairing.
