products.name: leave_request
products.description: Employee leave and absence requests — including leave type (annual, sick, parental, unpaid, FMLA), requested dates, approved dates, leave status, approver, and impact on project allocations. Sourced from Workday HCM Absence Management. Feeds into capacity planning and resource availability calculations.

attributes.name: leave_request_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each employee leave and absence request record in the Workday HCM Absence Management module. Serves as the primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: approver_employee_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the manager or HR representative who reviewed and approved or rejected this leave request. Supports approval workflow tracking and accountability.

attributes.name: initiative_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary Workfront project most impacted by this leave request. Enables direct linkage between absence management and project resource allocation, supporting capacity planning and WIP (Work in Progress) management for advertising campaigns.
attributes.references: Workfront Project Management; Workday HCM Absence Management

attributes.name: primary_leave_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee (Full-Time Equivalent, freelancer, contractor, or production crew member) who submitted this leave request. Links to the talent/employee master record.

attributes.name: actual_return_date
attributes.description: The actual date the employee returned to work, which may differ from the planned return_to_work_date due to early return, extension, or medical clearance requirements. Used for reconciling capacity plans and updating resource availability in Workfront.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; Workfront Resource Management

attributes.name: approval_notes
attributes.description: Free-text comments entered by the approver during the review process, documenting conditions, modifications, or reasons for approval or rejection. Sourced from Workday HCM Absence Management workflow comments.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the approver formally approved or rejected the leave request in Workday HCM. Null if the request is still pending or has been withdrawn.

attributes.name: approved_duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of working days formally approved for the leave period. May differ from requested_duration_days if the approver modified the leave window or partial approval was granted.

attributes.name: approved_end_date
attributes.description: The last calendar date of the leave period as formally approved. May differ from the requested end date if the approver modified the leave window.

attributes.name: approved_start_date
attributes.description: The first calendar date of the leave period as formally approved by the manager or HR. May differ from the requested start date if the approver modified the leave window.

attributes.name: backfill_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a temporary replacement (freelancer, contractor, or internal reallocation) is required to cover the employee's responsibilities during the leave period. Triggers talent acquisition or resource reallocation workflows.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Talent Management; Workfront Resource Management

attributes.name: backfill_type
attributes.description: The type of resource used to cover the employee's responsibilities during the leave period. Supports financial reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA and talent cost tracking for the P&L (Profit and Loss) of the talent domain.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Talent Management; SAP S/4HANA CO

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: The reason provided when a leave request is cancelled or withdrawn, either by the employee or by HR. Populated only when request_status is 'cancelled' or 'withdrawn'. Supports HR audit trails and leave management reporting.

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The SAP S/4HANA CO cost center code associated with the employee's organizational unit. Used for financial allocation of leave costs and payroll charges during the absence period.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO; Workday HCM Core HR

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this leave request record was first created in the source system (Workday HCM). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: department_name
attributes.description: The name of the organizational department to which the employee belongs at the time of the leave request, as recorded in Workday HCM. Used for HR reporting, capacity planning by department, and resource availability dashboards.

attributes.name: employee_notes
attributes.description: Free-text comments entered by the employee when submitting the leave request, providing additional context or supporting information. May contain sensitive personal information; classified as confidential per GDPR Article 5 data minimisation principles.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; GDPR Article 5; CCPA

attributes.name: intermittent_leave
attributes.description: Indicates whether the leave is taken intermittently (non-consecutive days or partial days) rather than as a continuous block. Common for FMLA qualifying conditions. Affects capacity planning granularity and Workfront resource scheduling.

attributes.name: is_fmla_qualifying
attributes.business_glossary_term: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Qualifying Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this leave request qualifies under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), entitling the employee to job-protected unpaid leave. Relevant for US-based employees. Drives compliance reporting and payroll processing in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act); Workday HCM Absence Management

attributes.name: is_paid
attributes.description: Indicates whether the approved leave is paid (True) or unpaid (False). Drives payroll processing in Workday HCM Payroll and SAP S/4HANA FI/CO for accurate compensation calculations during the leave period.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Payroll; SAP S/4HANA FI

attributes.name: job_profile
attributes.description: The employee's job profile or role title as defined in Workday HCM at the time of the leave request (e.g., Creative Director, Media Planner, Account Manager, FTE). Used to assess skill-based resource impact and inform backfill sourcing decisions.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Core HR; Workday HCM Talent Management

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this leave request record was most recently updated in the source system (Workday HCM). Supports change detection and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: leave_balance_after_days
attributes.description: The employee's remaining leave balance in days for the applicable leave type after the approved leave is deducted. Sourced from Workday HCM Absence Management. Used for capacity planning and leave entitlement monitoring.

attributes.name: leave_balance_before_days
attributes.description: The employee's available leave balance in days for the applicable leave type at the time the request was submitted. Sourced from Workday HCM Absence Management leave accrual records. Supports leave entitlement validation and HR reporting.

attributes.name: leave_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason provided by the employee for the leave request, as captured in Workday HCM. May contain sensitive health or personal information; classified as confidential. Used for HR reporting and compliance with FMLA and GDPR Article 9 sensitive data provisions.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; FMLA; GDPR Article 9; CCPA

attributes.name: leave_subtype
attributes.description: Further classification within a leave type, such as maternity, paternity, or adoption under parental leave; or short-term versus long-term under sick leave. Sourced from Workday HCM Absence Management leave plan configuration.

attributes.name: leave_type
attributes.description: Classification of the leave request by category as defined in Workday HCM Absence Management. Common types include annual (vacation), sick, parental, unpaid, FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act), and bereavement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: annual|sick|parental|unpaid|fmla|bereavement|jury_duty|military|sabbatical|personal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act); GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: medical_certification_received
attributes.description: Indicates whether the required medical certification or documentation has been received and validated by HR. Null or False when medical_certification_required is False. Supports FMLA compliance tracking and leave approval gating.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; FMLA; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: medical_certification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a medical certificate or healthcare provider documentation is required to support this leave request (e.g., for extended sick leave or FMLA qualifying events). Drives HR compliance workflows in Workday HCM.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; FMLA; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: request_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the leave request within the Workday HCM approval workflow. Drives capacity planning and resource availability calculations in Workfront resource management.

attributes.name: requested_duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of working days requested for the leave period, as calculated by Workday HCM based on the employee's work schedule and calendar. Supports capacity planning and leave balance deduction calculations.

attributes.name: requested_end_date
attributes.description: The last calendar date of the leave period as requested by the employee. Combined with requested_start_date to determine the total requested leave duration.

attributes.name: requested_start_date
attributes.description: The first calendar date of the leave period as requested by the employee. Used for scheduling, capacity planning, and project allocation impact assessment in Workfront.

attributes.name: resource_impact_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the operational impact this leave request has on active campaign projects and resource allocations in Workfront. Levels range from none (no active project assignments) to critical (key FTE on active campaign delivery). Informs backfill and freelancer sourcing decisions.
attributes.references: Workfront Resource Management; Workday HCM Absence Management

attributes.name: return_to_work_date
attributes.description: The confirmed or expected date on which the employee is scheduled to return to active work following the leave period. Critical for resource availability calculations in Workfront and capacity planning for campaign and production teams.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; Workfront Resource Management

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the originating system from which this leave request record was sourced into the Databricks Silver Layer. Primarily Workday HCM Absence Management, but may include manual entries or API integrations for legacy data migration.
attributes.references: Workday HCM Absence Management; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the employee formally submitted the leave request in Workday HCM. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: workday_absence_request_reference
attributes.description: The externally-known unique identifier assigned by Workday HCM Absence Management to this leave request. Used for cross-system traceability and reconciliation with the source system of record.

attributes.name: worker_type
attributes.description: Classification of the employee's engagement type within the agency workforce as defined in Workday HCM. Determines applicable leave entitlements, payroll treatment, and regulatory compliance requirements (e.g., FMLA eligibility for FTEs). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fte|freelancer|contractor|influencer|actor|photographer|director|production_crew — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Workday HCM Core HR; FMLA; GDPR Article 4

products.name: performance_review

attributes.name: performance_review_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formal talent performance evaluation record in the Workday HCM Talent Management module.

attributes.name: brand_profile_id

attributes.description: Reference to the talent record of the employee being evaluated in this performance review cycle.

attributes.name: review_cycle_id
attributes.description: Reference to the performance review cycle definition (e.g., Annual FY2024, Mid-Year H1 2024, Probationary 90-Day) under which this evaluation was conducted.

attributes.name: reviewer_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the talent record of the manager or designated reviewer who conducted and submitted this performance evaluation.

attributes.name: calibrated_rating

attributes.description: Average numeric score across all evaluated competency dimensions (e.g., strategic thinking, client service, creative excellence, collaboration, leadership) for this review period.

attributes.name: completion_date

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: creative_excellence_score

attributes.name: development_areas_summary

attributes.name: digital_analytics_score

attributes.name: employee_acknowledgement_date

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: leadership_competency_score

attributes.name: merit_increase_pct

attributes.name: merit_increase_recommended

products.name: talent_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of agency workforce members to project initiatives. It captures the operational reality of resource allocation, tracking which workers are assigned to which projects, in what capacity, for what duration, and at what rates. Each record links one worker to one initiative with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific assignment relationship—role, dates, hours, allocation percentage, and billing/cost rates.. Existence Justification: In advertising agency operations, workers are routinely assigned to multiple concurrent initiatives (an account director may oversee 5 campaigns simultaneously, a designer may contribute to 3 projects), and initiatives require multiple workers across creative, account, and production teams. The detection reasoning explicitly states that 'the assignment relationship tracks role, dates, hours, rates, and billability—all relationship-specific data' and notes that the business calls this 'project assignment' or 'resource assignment.' This is a textbook operational M:N relationship where the assignment itself is a managed business entity.

attributes.name: talent_assignment_id
attributes.description: Primary key for talent_assignment

attributes.name: initiative_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to project.initiative identifying the project to which the worker is assigned.

attributes.name: worker_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to talent.worker identifying the workforce member assigned to this initiative.

attributes.name: actual_hours
attributes.description: The cumulative actual hours worked by this worker on this initiative, typically sourced from time tracking systems (Workfront, Monday.com, or timesheets). Updated continuously as time is logged.

attributes.name: allocation_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the worker's total capacity allocated to this initiative (e.g., 50.00 means half-time). Used for resource utilization tracking and capacity planning. Sum of all concurrent allocations for a worker should not exceed 100% in healthy resource plans.

attributes.name: assignment_code
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each worker-to-initiative assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this assignment. Planned = forecasted but not yet started; Active = worker currently engaged; On Hold = temporarily paused; Completed = assignment finished; Cancelled = assignment terminated before completion.

attributes.name: billable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this worker's time on this initiative is billable to the client (true) or non-billable/internal (false). Drives revenue recognition and client invoicing. May differ from initiative.is_billable if specific roles are non-billable on an otherwise billable project.

attributes.name: billing_rate
attributes.description: The hourly or daily rate at which this worker's time is billed to the client for this specific initiative. May differ from the worker's standard pay rate and can vary by project, client, or contract terms. Used for revenue calculation and client invoicing.

attributes.name: cost_rate
attributes.description: The internal cost rate for this worker on this initiative, used for project profitability analysis and margin calculation. Typically derived from the worker's pay_rate plus burden (benefits, overhead allocation). May be assignment-specific if special compensation applies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this assignment record was created in the source system or data platform.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The planned or actual date when the worker's assignment to this initiative ends. May be null for ongoing assignments. Used for resource forecasting and assignment lifecycle management.

attributes.name: planned_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours planned or budgeted for this worker on this initiative. Used for capacity planning, budget estimation, and variance analysis against actual hours.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level of this assignment relative to the worker's other concurrent assignments. Used for resource conflict resolution and workload balancing when a worker is over-allocated.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: The specific role or function the worker performs on this initiative (e.g., Creative Director, Account Manager, Designer, Media Planner). This is assignment-specific and may differ from the worker's job title—a Senior Designer may serve as Lead Designer on one project and Contributing Designer on another.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: The unique assignment or resource allocation identifier from the originating project management system (Workfront, Monday.com). Used for data lineage and system reconciliation.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when the worker's assignment to this initiative begins. Used for resource planning, availability tracking, and billing period determination.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this assignment record was last modified in the source system or data platform.

products.name: representation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual representation relationship between talent profiles and supplier agencies in the advertising ecosystem. It captures the commercial terms, territorial scope, and lifecycle of representation agreements. Each record links one talent_profile to one supplier (talent agency, management firm) with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific representation contract, including commission structures, exclusivity terms, territory restrictions, and representation periods.. Existence Justification: In the advertising industry, talent (actors, influencers, models, directors, creatives) are commonly represented by multiple agencies simultaneously for different geographic territories, media types, or under non-exclusive arrangements. Conversely, each talent agency or management firm (supplier) represents many talent profiles. The representation relationship is a contractual business entity with specific commercial terms (commission rates, exclusivity scope, territory restrictions) that vary by each talent-agency pairing and cannot be stored on either entity alone.

attributes.name: representation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the representation agreement record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: supplier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the supplier (talent agency or management firm) providing representation

attributes.name: talent_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the talent profile being represented

attributes.name: commission_rate
attributes.description: The commission percentage charged by the supplier agency for bookings made under this representation agreement, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.15 for 15%). Varies by supplier-talent combination based on negotiated terms.

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: External reference number or identifier for the legal representation contract document stored in the contract management system or document repository.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the representation agreement record was created in the data platform.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The termination or expiry date of the representation agreement. Null indicates an open-ended or currently active agreement. Used for historical tracking and commission cutoff.

attributes.name: exclusivity_scope
attributes.description: Defines the exclusivity terms of the representation agreement. Values: exclusive (sole representation across all markets), non_exclusive (talent can have multiple agencies), category_exclusive (exclusive within specific industry verticals), territory_exclusive (exclusive within defined geographic territories).

attributes.name: primary_contact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this supplier is the primary or preferred agency contact for the talent when multiple non-exclusive representation agreements exist. Used to route initial booking inquiries and campaign briefs.

attributes.name: representation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the representation agreement. Values: active (currently in force), suspended (temporarily inactive), terminated (ended), pending (signed but not yet effective). Only active agreements are used for commission calculation and booking workflow.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The effective start date of the representation agreement. Used to determine active representation periods for talent booking and commission calculation.

attributes.name: territory_restrictions
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or region identifiers defining the geographic scope of the representation agreement (e.g., USA|CAN|MEX for North America). Used to determine which agency to contact for bookings in specific markets.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the representation agreement record was last modified in the data platform.

attributes.name: holiday_calendar_id

attributes.description: Reference to the organization or business unit that owns and uses this holiday calendar. Applicable for organizational and production calendars; nullable for national/regional calendars.

attributes.name: applies_to_contractors
attributes.description: Indicates whether this holiday calendar applies to contractors and freelancers. True if contractors observe these holidays; false if they follow different schedules.

attributes.name: applies_to_full_time_employees
attributes.description: Indicates whether this holiday calendar applies to full-time employees. True if FTE staff observe these holidays; false if excluded.

attributes.name: applies_to_production_crew
attributes.description: Indicates whether this holiday calendar applies to production crews (directors, photographers, actors, production staff). True if production schedules must respect these holidays; false if production operates independently.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this holiday calendar was formally approved for use in resource planning, payroll, and time tracking systems.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the person or role who approved this holiday calendar for use. Typically an HR manager, operations director, or authorized administrator.

attributes.name: calendar_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the calendar for system integration and reference (e.g., 'US_FED_2024', 'UK_BANK', 'PROD_CAL').

attributes.name: calendar_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name of the holiday calendar (e.g., 'US Federal Holidays 2024', 'UK Bank Holidays', 'Agency Production Calendar').

attributes.name: calendar_type
attributes.description: Classification of the holiday calendar indicating its scope and purpose: national (country-wide public holidays), regional (state/province holidays), organizational (company-specific holidays), production (shoot/production blackout dates), project (campaign-specific non-working days).

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the primary country jurisdiction for this holiday calendar (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN, FRA). Used for national and regional calendars.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this holiday calendar record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the purpose, scope, and applicability of this holiday calendar, including any special rules or exceptions.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The last date on which this holiday calendar is applicable. Nullable for open-ended calendars that remain in effect until superseded.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The first date on which this holiday calendar becomes applicable for resource planning, payroll, and time tracking purposes.

attributes.name: external_calendar_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this holiday calendar in the source system (e.g., Workday calendar ID, Workfront calendar GUID). Used for integration and synchronization with upstream systems.

attributes.name: is_default
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the default holiday calendar for the organization or region. True if this calendar should be automatically applied to new employees or projects; false otherwise.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this holiday calendar record was last updated. Used for change tracking and synchronization with downstream systems.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or exceptions related to this holiday calendar (e.g., 'Includes floating holidays', 'Production blackout dates for Q4 campaign').

attributes.name: observance_rule
attributes.description: Defines how holidays that fall on weekends are observed. Values: actual_date (holiday observed on the actual date regardless of day of week), nearest_weekday (shifted to nearest weekday), following_monday (shifted to following Monday if on weekend), preceding_friday (shifted to preceding Friday if on weekend).

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: State, province, or regional subdivision code for calendars that apply to specific geographic regions within a country (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'ON' for Ontario, 'NSW' for New South Wales). Nullable for national or organizational calendars.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The system of record from which this holiday calendar was sourced or integrated (e.g., 'Workday HCM', 'Workfront', 'Manual Entry', 'Government API'). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the holiday calendar. Active calendars are in use for resource planning and time tracking; draft calendars are under review; inactive calendars are temporarily disabled; archived calendars are retained for historical reference only.

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for this holiday calendar (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Tokyo'). Used to determine exact holiday start/end times for global operations.

attributes.name: total_holidays
attributes.description: The total number of distinct holiday dates defined in this calendar. Used for quick reference and capacity planning calculations.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number for this holiday calendar. Incremented each time the calendar is updated or revised. Supports change tracking and audit history.

attributes.name: weekend_pattern
attributes.description: Defines the standard weekend days for this calendar. Values: sat_sun (Saturday and Sunday, common in Western countries), fri_sat (Friday and Saturday, common in Middle East), sun_only (Sunday only), none (no standard weekend, e.g., shift-based operations).

attributes.name: working_days_per_year
attributes.description: The calculated number of working days in the calendar year after excluding weekends and holidays. Used for resource capacity planning, project scheduling, and workload forecasting.

attributes.name: year
attributes.description: The calendar year (YYYY) for which this holiday calendar is defined. Many organizations maintain separate calendar records per year to accommodate year-specific holiday variations.

attributes.name: derived_from_holiday_calendar_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on holiday_calendar (derived_from_holiday_calendar_id)

attributes.name: calendar_type

attributes.name: country_code

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: default_pay_date_offset_days

attributes.name: description

attributes.name: effective_end_date

attributes.name: effective_start_date

attributes.name: first_pay_period_start_date

attributes.name: fiscal_year

attributes.name: holiday_calendar_id

attributes.name: is_default_calendar

attributes.name: is_locked

attributes.name: last_pay_period_end_date

attributes.name: locked_timestamp

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: pay_frequency

attributes.name: region_code

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the payroll calendar indicating whether it is in use, archived, or under development.

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the payroll calendar (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') used for scheduling and cutoff times.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the payroll calendar to track changes and revisions over time.

attributes.name: workday_hcm_calendar_id

attributes.name: workfront_calendar_id

attributes.name: prior_payroll_calendar_id

attributes.name: doing_business_as_name

attributes.name: employee_count

attributes.name: is_tax_exempt

attributes.name: jurisdiction_country_code

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state_province

attributes.name: legal_name

attributes.name: lei_code

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: ownership_percentage

attributes.name: website_url

domains.name: performance
domains.description: Operational domain capturing real-time and near-real-time campaign delivery metrics and performance signals — including impressions, clicks, conversions, ROAS, CPA, CTR, SOV, and viewability. Owns raw delivery event data and KPI actuals at the placement and line-item level. Distinct from analytics aggregations: focuses on operational measurement infrastructure, tracking pixels, conversion tags, and data quality validation.
domains.references: MRC Viewability and Impression Measurement Standards

products.name: impression_event
products.description: Raw delivery event record capturing each individual ad impression served across all channels and placements. Stores the atomic unit of campaign delivery — timestamp, placement, creative, device, geo, and auction-level signals from ad servers (Google Campaign Manager 360) and DSPs (The Trade Desk). Foundation for all downstream delivery measurement and billing reconciliation. Distinct from aggregated metrics: this is the raw event log at the impression grain.

attributes.name: impression_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each individual ad impression event. Primary key for the impression event log. Serves as the atomic unit for all downstream delivery measurement, billing reconciliation, and performance analytics.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Digital Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: activation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.audience_activation. Business justification: Activations push audience segments to DSPs/platforms where impressions are served. Links impression delivery to the specific activation job, enables match rate analysis, activation performance measure

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertiser client on whose behalf this impression was served. Enables client-level reporting and cross-campaign analysis.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.segment. Business justification: Core targeting relationship - every impression is served to a targeted audience segment. Essential for segment performance reporting, ROAS analysis, and optimization decisions. Fundamental to campaign

attributes.name: brand_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to brand.brand_profile. Business justification: Ad servers must track which brand profile each impression serves for brand safety compliance, consent management, and brand-level performance reporting. Essential for GARM/brand safety floor enforceme

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent advertising campaign under which this impression was served. Enables campaign-level aggregation and performance rollup.

attributes.name: client_brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_brand. Business justification: Brand-level performance reporting is core to advertising operations. Brand managers and clients require impression delivery metrics aggregated by brand for campaign optimization, media mix analysis, a

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the creative asset that was displayed in this impression. Links to creative master data containing asset specifications, format, dimensions, and approval status.

attributes.name: holdout_group_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.holdout_group. Business justification: Holdout groups define control populations that should NOT receive impressions for incrementality testing. Essential for measuring true advertising lift, validating campaign effectiveness, and calculat

attributes.name: line_item_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media plan line item or insertion order line that governs this impression delivery. Critical for pacing, budget tracking, and billing reconciliation.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Insertion Order Standards

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific media placement where this impression was delivered. Links to the media placement master data defining publisher, site, position, and format.

attributes.name: programmatic_deal_id
attributes.description: The identifier for the programmatic guaranteed deal, private marketplace (PMP) deal, or preferred deal under which this impression was transacted. Links to deal master data for supply-path analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Programmatic Deal Standards

attributes.name: publisher_id
attributes.description: Reference to the publisher or media property where the impression was delivered. Links to publisher master data for supply-side analysis and reconciliation.

attributes.name: suppression_list_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.suppression_list. Business justification: Impressions must respect suppression lists (frequency caps, opt-outs, competitive exclusions). Critical for compliance with privacy regulations, honoring user preferences, and preventing over-exposure

attributes.name: trafficking_instruction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trafficking instruction that governed the delivery of this impression. Links to ad server trafficking configuration for delivery validation and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: vendor_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.vendor_contract. Business justification: Vendor contracts with publishers/SSPs govern inventory supply terms and rates. Linking impressions to vendor contracts enables rate reconciliation, volume commitment tracking, and supplier performance

attributes.name: ad_position
attributes.description: The position of the ad unit on the page or within the app. Indicates placement prominence and impacts viewability and engagement rates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: above_the_fold|below_the_fold|header|footer|sidebar|in_content|interstitial|overlay — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Ad Placement Standards

attributes.name: ad_server_source
attributes.description: The ad serving platform or demand-side platform (DSP) that recorded and delivered this impression. Identifies the operational system of record for this event.

attributes.name: ad_size
attributes.description: The pixel dimensions of the ad creative served (e.g., 300x250, 728x90, 1920x1080). Used for format performance analysis and creative optimization.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Universal Ad Package Standards

attributes.name: auction_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the programmatic auction in which this impression was won. Used for RTB (Real-Time Bidding) analysis, bid landscape reconstruction, and supply-path optimization.

attributes.name: audience_segment_ids
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of audience segment IDs that the user matched at impression time. Links to audience taxonomy from DMP (Data Management Platform) or CDP (Customer Data Platform). Used for audience targeting validation and performance analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Audience Taxonomy Standards

attributes.name: bid_price_cpm
attributes.description: The winning bid price for this impression expressed in CPM (Cost Per Mille / cost per thousand impressions). Represents the clearing price in the programmatic auction. Used for media cost analysis and ROAS calculation.

attributes.name: brand_safety_score
attributes.description: A score from 0.00 to 100.00 indicating the brand safety level of the content context where the impression was served. Higher scores indicate safer, more brand-appropriate environments.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Brand Safety Standards; TAG (Trustworthy Accountability Group) - Brand Safety Certification

attributes.name: browser
attributes.description: The web browser or app environment in which the impression was displayed (e.g., Chrome, Safari, Firefox, in-app). Used for browser-specific performance and compatibility analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - User Agent Standards

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The digital channel or device environment where the impression was delivered. Includes desktop web, mobile web, mobile app, Connected TV (CTV), Over-the-Top (OTT), and Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH).

attributes.name: consent_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether user consent was obtained for data collection and ad personalization at impression time. Critical for GDPR and CCPA compliance. Values: granted (consent obtained), denied (consent refused), not_required (jurisdiction does not require consent), unknown (consent status not captured).
attributes.references: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 7; CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act); IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF)

attributes.name: content_category
attributes.description: The IAB content category or taxonomy classification of the page or app content where the impression was served. Used for contextual targeting validation and brand safety analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Content Taxonomy Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the media cost and bid price. Enables multi-currency campaign analysis and financial reconciliation.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: The category of device on which the impression was rendered. Used for device-level performance analysis and cross-device attribution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: desktop|smartphone|tablet|smart_tv|gaming_console|wearable|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Device Classification Standards

attributes.name: event_source_system
attributes.description: The name and version of the source system that generated this impression event record. Used for data lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation.

attributes.name: fraud_score
attributes.description: A risk score from 0.00 to 100.00 indicating the likelihood that this impression is fraudulent or invalid. Generated by fraud detection vendors or internal algorithms. Higher scores indicate higher fraud risk.
attributes.references: TAG (Trustworthy Accountability Group) - Fraud Detection Standards

attributes.name: frequency_cap_count
attributes.description: The number of times this user has been exposed to this campaign or creative prior to this impression. Used for frequency capping enforcement and ad fatigue analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Frequency Management Standards

attributes.name: geo_city
attributes.description: The city or designated market area (DMA) where the impression was delivered. Enables hyper-local targeting validation and metro-level performance analysis.

attributes.name: geo_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the geographic location where the impression was delivered. Derived from IP geolocation or device GPS. Used for geo-targeting validation and regional performance analysis.

attributes.name: geo_postal_code
attributes.description: The postal or ZIP code where the impression was delivered. Supports neighborhood-level targeting and local market analysis.

attributes.name: geo_region
attributes.description: The state, province, or region where the impression was delivered. Supports sub-national geographic analysis and local market performance tracking.

attributes.name: impression_timestamp
attributes.description: Exact date and time when the ad impression was served to the end user. Represents the real-world event time of ad delivery. Critical for time-series analysis, dayparting optimization, and billing reconciliation. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Ad Serving Timestamp Standards

attributes.name: impression_type
attributes.description: The format or modality of the ad impression served. Distinguishes between display banners, video ads, native content, audio spots, and rich media executions.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Ad Format Standards

attributes.name: ingestion_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this impression event record was ingested into the lakehouse silver layer. Used for data freshness monitoring and ETL (Extract Transform Load) pipeline auditing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: ip_address
attributes.description: The IP address of the device that received the impression. Used for geo-targeting validation, fraud detection, and audience verification. May be considered PII under GDPR and CCPA.
attributes.references: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 4; CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act)

attributes.name: is_autoplay
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the video ad started playing automatically without user initiation. Applicable to video impressions. Impacts user experience and engagement metrics.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) Standards

attributes.name: is_bot_traffic
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the impression was identified as non-human bot traffic. Used for invalid traffic (IVT) filtering and billing adjustment.
attributes.references: TAG (Trustworthy Accountability Group) - Invalid Traffic (IVT) Standards; MRC (Media Rating Council) - Invalid Traffic Detection

attributes.name: is_muted
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the video or audio ad was muted at the time of impression. Applicable to video and audio impression types. Impacts engagement and completion rates.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) Standards

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: The latitude coordinate of the impression delivery location. Used for proximity-based targeting validation and location-based analytics, particularly for DOOH and mobile campaigns.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: The longitude coordinate of the impression delivery location. Used for proximity-based targeting validation and location-based analytics, particularly for DOOH and mobile campaigns.

attributes.name: media_cost
attributes.description: The actual media cost incurred for this single impression. Calculated from the bid price or rate card. Used for billing reconciliation, budget tracking, and ROI (Return on Investment) analysis.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Ad Serving and Billing Standards

attributes.name: operating_system
attributes.description: The operating system of the device that rendered the impression (e.g., iOS, Android, Windows, macOS). Supports device compatibility analysis and targeting optimization.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - User Agent Standards

attributes.name: page_url
attributes.description: The full URL of the page where the impression was displayed. Supports contextual analysis, brand safety verification, and content alignment validation.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Content Taxonomy Standards

attributes.name: session_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the user session during which this impression was served. Enables session-level analysis and cross-impression journey tracking.

attributes.name: site_domain
attributes.description: The domain name of the website or app where the impression was served. Used for brand safety analysis, contextual targeting validation, and publisher performance tracking.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Content Taxonomy Standards

attributes.name: supply_chain_object
attributes.description: The sellers.json or SupplyChain object captured at impression time, identifying all intermediaries in the programmatic supply chain. Used for supply-path transparency and optimization per IAB ads.txt and sellers.json standards.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Ads.txt and Sellers.json Standards

attributes.name: tcf_consent_string
attributes.business_glossary_term: Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF) Consent String
attributes.description: The IAB Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF) consent string captured at impression time. Encodes user consent choices for data processing purposes. Required for GDPR compliance in programmatic advertising.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF) v2.0; GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)

attributes.name: time_in_view_seconds
attributes.description: The total duration in seconds that the impression was visible in the users viewport. Critical metric for engagement analysis and viewability quality assessment.
attributes.references: MRC (Media Rating Council) - Viewable Impression Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: user_agent
attributes.description: The full user agent string captured at impression time. Contains detailed device, browser, and operating system information for advanced device fingerprinting and fraud detection.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - User Agent Standards

attributes.name: user_identifier
attributes.description: The pseudonymized or hashed user identifier (cookie ID, device ID, or universal ID) associated with this impression. Used for cross-device tracking, frequency management, and attribution. Subject to GDPR and CCPA privacy regulations.
attributes.references: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 4; CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act); IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - User ID Standards

attributes.name: video_duration_seconds
attributes.description: The total duration of the video ad creative in seconds. Applicable only to video impression types. Used for video completion rate analysis and engagement measurement.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) Standards

attributes.name: video_player_size
attributes.description: The size category of the video player at impression time. Applicable to video impressions. Impacts viewability and user engagement.
attributes.references: IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) Standards

attributes.name: viewability_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the ad creative that was visible in the viewport at the time of measurement. Ranges from 0.00 to 100.00. Used for granular viewability analysis and quality scoring.
attributes.references: MRC (Media Rating Council) - Viewable Impression Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: viewability_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the impression met the MRC (Media Rating Council) viewability standard at the time of delivery. Viewable means the ad was in-view per IAB/MRC guidelines (50% of pixels visible for 1+ seconds for display, 2+ seconds for video).
attributes.references: MRC (Media Rating Council) - Viewable Impression Measurement Guidelines; IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau) - Viewability Standards

products.name: click_event
products.description: Raw click interaction event record capturing each user click on a served ad unit. Stores click timestamp, placement identifier, creative identifier, redirect URL, device fingerprint, and click validation status (invalid traffic / IVT flags per TAG/MRC standards). Source of CPC billing actuals and CTR computation inputs. Distinct from impression_event: represents a user-initiated interaction, not a passive delivery.

attributes.name: click_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each click event record. Primary key for the click event entity.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Digital Ad Event Standards

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.segment. Business justification: Clicks occur within targeted segments - critical for segment-level CTR analysis, engagement measurement, and audience quality scoring. Enables advertisers to identify high-performing segments and opti

attributes.name: brand_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to brand.brand_profile. Business justification: Click attribution and engagement analysis require brand context for brand-level CTR reporting, brand engagement dashboards, and multi-brand advertiser performance comparison. Standard in enterprise ad

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertising campaign under which this click occurred. Enables campaign-level click aggregation and performance analysis.

attributes.name: contract_insertion_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.insertion_order. Business justification: CPC-based IOs require click-level tracking for budget consumption and invoice reconciliation. Enables automated billing validation against contracted click rates and caps. Essential for performance-ba

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the creative asset that was clicked. Identifies the specific ad unit, banner, video, or interactive element that received the user interaction.

attributes.name: impression_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent impression event that was served before this click occurred. Links click to the originating ad delivery event.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Digital Ad Event Standards

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media placement where the clicked ad was served. Identifies the specific inventory position and publisher context.

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the user session during which the click occurred. Enables session-level analysis and multi-touch attribution within a single browsing session.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Session Tracking Standards

attributes.name: ad_server_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the ad server that recorded and tracked this click event (e.g., Google Campaign Manager 360, Sizmek, Flashtalking). Used for data reconciliation and discrepancy analysis.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Ad Serving Standards

attributes.name: attribution_window_hours
attributes.description: The number of hours after the click during which a conversion can be attributed to this click event. Typically set at campaign or advertiser level (e.g., 24, 72, 168 hours).

attributes.name: billing_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this click event is billable under the cost-per-click (CPC) pricing model. Non-billable clicks include invalid traffic, duplicate clicks, and clicks outside contracted parameters.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Billing Standards; MRC Viewability Guidelines

attributes.name: click_fraud_score
attributes.description: Numeric fraud risk score assigned by the invalid traffic detection system, typically ranging from 0 (legitimate) to 100 (high fraud risk). Used for sophisticated IVT filtering and billing dispute resolution.
attributes.references: TAG Invalid Traffic Guidelines; MRC IVT Standards

attributes.name: click_interaction_type
attributes.description: The type of user interaction that triggered the click event. Distinguishes between standard clicks, video overlay clicks, expandable ad interactions, and mobile gestures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard_click|call_to_action|video_overlay|expandable_panel|swipe|tap|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Rich Media Guidelines

attributes.name: click_latency_ms
attributes.description: Time elapsed in milliseconds between the impression render and the click event. Used to detect rapid-fire bot clicks and analyze user engagement timing patterns.

attributes.name: click_position_x
attributes.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate of the click within the ad unit. Used for heatmap analysis and creative engagement optimization.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Creative Interaction Standards

attributes.name: click_position_y
attributes.description: Vertical pixel coordinate of the click within the ad unit. Used for heatmap analysis and creative engagement optimization.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Creative Interaction Standards

attributes.name: click_redirect_url
attributes.description: The destination URL to which the user was redirected after clicking the ad. May include tracking parameters, campaign identifiers, and attribution tokens.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Click Tracking Standards

attributes.name: click_source_platform
attributes.description: The platform or channel through which the click was delivered. Distinguishes between web, mobile app, connected TV (CTV), digital out-of-home (DOOH), and other channels. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: web|mobile_web|mobile_app|ctv|dooh|email|social|search|other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: click_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the user clicked the ad unit, captured in UTC. Primary business event timestamp for click-through rate (CTR) calculation and time-series analysis.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab - Event Timestamp Standards

attributes.name: click_validation_status
attributes.description: Validation status indicating whether the click is considered legitimate traffic or flagged as invalid per TAG (Trustworthy Accountability Group) and MRC (Media Rating Council) invalid traffic (IVT) detection standards. Determines billability for cost-per-click (CPC) campaigns. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: valid|invalid_bot|invalid_duplicate|invalid_fraud|invalid_datacenter|suspicious|pending_validation — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: TAG Invalid Traffic (IVT) Guidelines; MRC Invalid Traffic Detection Standards

attributes.name: conversion_attributed_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this click event was later attributed to a conversion event within the attribution window. Used for click-to-conversion analysis and return on ad spend (ROAS) calculation.

attributes.name: cpc_rate
attributes.description: The contracted cost per click rate for this event in the campaign currency. Used to calculate click-level revenue and cost-per-acquisition (CPA) metrics.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the CPC rate and billing amounts. Supports multi-currency campaign reconciliation.

products.name: tracking_pixel
products.description: Master record and complete operational event log for each tracking pixel or conversion tag deployed on advertiser web properties, app environments, or landing pages. Header section stores pixel definition: name, type (impression tracker, click tracker, conversion tag, retargeting pixel, audience pixel), implementation method (JavaScript, image pixel, server-to-server), firing rules, consent flags, and deployment status. Detail section stores the complete fire event history: individual fire timestamps, firing URL, user agent, IP hash (GDPR-compliant), referrer URL, custom parameters passed, fire status (success/blocked/timeout), and error details. Single source of truth for all pixel infrastructure configuration AND raw fire event data. Serves as the unified measurement infrastructure registry, pixel health monitoring source, and raw fire event stream for conversion deduplication and data quality validation. Supports GDPR/CCPA consent compliance workflows and tag governance audits.

products.description: Real-time and near-real-time delivery pacing record tracking actual vs. planned delivery progress for each campaign line item and placement. Stores pacing period (hourly, daily), planned impression/spend target, actual delivered impressions/spend, pacing percentage, pacing status (on-pace, under-delivering, over-delivering), and recommended bid/budget adjustment signals. Sourced from Google Campaign Manager 360 and The Trade Desk pacing APIs. Critical for operational campaign management and budget stewardship.

attributes.description: The actual number of impressions delivered during this pacing period as reported by the ad server or demand-side platform (DSP).

attributes.description: The percentage of impressions that resulted in clicks during this pacing period, calculated as (clicks / impressions) * 100. Key performance indicator for engagement.

attributes.name: delivery_method
attributes.description: The delivery pacing strategy configured for this line item. Standard spreads delivery evenly, accelerated delivers as fast as possible, even maintains consistent daily delivery, ASAP prioritizes immediate delivery, frontloaded concentrates delivery early in the flight.

attributes.name: effective_cpa
attributes.description: The effective cost per conversion for this pacing period, calculated as actual_spend_amount / conversion_count. Key metric for performance-based campaigns.

attributes.name: impression_pacing_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of planned impressions that have been delivered, calculated as (actual_impressions / planned_impressions) * 100. Values above 100 indicate over-delivery.

attributes.name: inventory_availability_score

attributes.name: pacing_status

attributes.name: pacing_variance_threshold
attributes.description: The acceptable variance threshold percentage used to determine pacing status. If actual pacing percentage deviates from 100% by more than this threshold, status changes from on-pace to under/over-delivering.

attributes.name: planned_impressions

attributes.name: planned_spend_amount

attributes.description: Platform-assigned quality score (typically 0-10 scale) reflecting ad relevance, landing page experience, and expected CTR. Higher scores improve auction competitiveness.

attributes.name: recommended_bid_adjustment
attributes.description: System-generated recommendation for bid adjustment to correct pacing issues. Positive values suggest increasing bids to accelerate delivery, negative values suggest decreasing bids to slow delivery.

attributes.name: recommended_budget_adjustment
attributes.description: System-generated recommendation for budget adjustment to correct pacing issues. Positive values suggest increasing budget allocation, negative values suggest reducing budget allocation.

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: The unique identifier of this pacing record in the source operational system, used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: spend_pacing_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of planned spend that has been consumed, calculated as (actual_spend_amount / planned_spend_amount) * 100. Values above 100 indicate over-spend.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this pacing record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer. Tracks data refresh cycles and enables incremental processing.

attributes.name: viewability_rate
attributes.description: The percentage of delivered impressions that met viewability standards (MRC: 50% of pixels in view for 1+ seconds for display, 2+ seconds for video) during this pacing period.

products.name: ivt_classification

Stores IVT type (bot traffic, data center traffic, hijacked device, adware), IVT detection source (TAG certified vendor, DSP internal, ad server), IVT volume, and financial impact (invalid spend). Used for media quality assurance, vendor chargebacks, and MRC compliance reporting.

attributes.name: ivt_classification_id

attributes.name: brand_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to brand.brand_profile. Business justification: Invalid traffic detection and chargeback processing is tracked per brand for brand protection, billing dispute resolution, and brand-level fraud reporting. Multi-brand advertisers require brand-specif

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the advertising campaign associated with this IVT event. Used for campaign-level IVT quality reporting.

attributes.name: click_event_id

attributes.name: impression_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to performance.impression_event. attributes.name: supplier_id

attributes.name: bot_signature_match

attributes.name: chargeback_eligible_flag

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: data_center_flag

attributes.name: device_fingerprint

attributes.name: ivt_detection_source

attributes.name: user_agent

attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab OpenRTB User Agent Field; W3C User Agent String Standard

Sourced from brand safety vendors (IAS, DoubleVerify, Oracle Moat) and DSP pre-bid filtering signals. Supports advertiser brand safety commitments and GARM compliance.

products.name: measurement_discrepancy
products.description: Unified data quality and measurement discrepancy management record for all performance data ingested from ad servers, DSPs, and third-party measurement vendors. Encompasses two operational workflows: (1) Automated data quality checks — completeness, consistency, deduplication, latency, and schema validations applied to incoming delivery data, with check type, severity, status (passed/failed/warning), affected source system, affected date range, and remediation action taken; (2) Formal count discrepancies — variances between ad server delivery counts (Google Campaign Manager 360) and media vendor/publisher reported counts, with discrepancy percentage, MRC 10% threshold breach flag, investigation status, root cause classification (tag latency, filtering methodology, timezone mismatch, IVT filtering delta), and financial resolution (credit, makegood, write-off). Single source of truth for all measurement quality issues. Supports media billing reconciliation, vendor accountability, MRC compliance audits, and operational data quality SLAs.

attributes.name: measurement_discrepancy_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the measurement discrepancy record. Primary key for the measurement discrepancy entity.

attributes.name: buy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media buy associated with this discrepancy. Links to the broader media purchase agreement.

attributes.name: media_placement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the media placement affected by this discrepancy. Links to the specific ad placement where the measurement variance occurred.

attributes.name: vendor_contact_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vendor_contact. Business justification: Discrepancy resolution requires tracking which vendor contact is handling investigation. Essential for SLA adherence tracking, escalation management, response time measurement, and maintaining audit t

attributes.name: vendor_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.vendor_contract. Business justification: Measurement discrepancies trigger financial reconciliation per vendor contract terms (MRC thresholds, dispute resolution). Direct link enables automated breach detection, financial adjustment calculat

attributes.name: affected_date_end
attributes.description: End date of the delivery data range affected by this discrepancy. Defines the conclusion of the time window where measurement variance or data quality issues occurred.

attributes.name: affected_date_start
attributes.description: Start date of the delivery data range affected by this discrepancy. Defines the beginning of the time window where measurement variance or data quality issues occurred.

attributes.name: audit_trail_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking to detailed audit logs, supporting documentation, email threads, or system logs related to the discrepancy investigation. Supports compliance audits and forensic analysis.
attributes.references: Internal Audit Policy; MRC Audit Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this measurement discrepancy record was first created in the system. Represents the audit trail creation time.

attributes.name: data_quality_check_status
attributes.description: Result status of the automated data quality validation. Passed indicates data met quality criteria. Failed indicates data did not meet criteria and requires remediation. Warning indicates potential issue requiring review. Skipped indicates check was not executed.

attributes.name: data_quality_check_type
attributes.description: For data quality check discrepancies, specifies the type of automated validation that failed. Completeness checks for missing required fields. Consistency checks for logical contradictions. Deduplication checks for duplicate events. Latency checks for delayed data arrival. Schema validation checks for structural conformance. Referential integrity checks for orphaned records.

attributes.name: data_quality_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the data quality issue. Critical indicates data unusable for billing or reporting. High indicates significant impact on accuracy. Medium indicates moderate impact requiring attention. Low indicates minor issue with minimal business impact.

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the discrepancy was first detected by automated monitoring systems or manual review. Represents the business event time of discovery.

attributes.name: discrepancy_count
attributes.description: Absolute difference between primary and secondary counts. Calculated as primary_count minus secondary_count. Positive values indicate over-delivery by secondary source; negative values indicate under-delivery.

attributes.name: discrepancy_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage variance between primary and secondary counts. Calculated as (discrepancy_count / primary_count) * 100. Used to assess materiality against MRC 10 percent threshold.

attributes.name: discrepancy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the discrepancy investigation and resolution workflow. Open indicates newly detected. Under investigation indicates active analysis. Resolved indicates root cause identified and remediation applied. Closed indicates final disposition complete. Escalated indicates elevated to senior management or vendor. Pending vendor indicates awaiting external party response.

attributes.name: discrepancy_type
attributes.description: Classification of the discrepancy. Count variance represents differences between ad server and vendor reported metrics. Data quality check represents automated validation failures. Latency issue represents delayed data delivery. Schema validation represents structural data problems. Deduplication represents duplicate event detection. Completeness check represents missing data detection.

attributes.name: financial_impact_amount
attributes.description: Monetary value of the discrepancy impact in the media buy currency. Calculated based on the discrepancy count multiplied by the contracted CPM, CPC, or CPA rate. Represents the dollar value at stake requiring financial resolution.

attributes.name: financial_resolution_type
attributes.description: Classification of the financial remedy applied to compensate for the measurement discrepancy. Credit represents monetary refund from vendor. Makegood represents additional ad delivery at no cost. Write-off represents agency absorbing the variance. No adjustment represents variance accepted within tolerance. Pending represents resolution not yet determined.
attributes.references: Internal Finance Policy; Mediaocean Billing Standards

attributes.name: investigation_assigned_to
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual or team assigned to investigate and resolve the discrepancy. Typically a media operations analyst, data quality engineer, or account manager.

attributes.name: investigation_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when formal investigation of the discrepancy began. Marks the transition from detection to active analysis.

attributes.name: metric_type
attributes.description: The performance metric type where the discrepancy occurred. Impressions represents ad delivery count. Clicks represents user interaction count. Conversions represents completed actions. Viewable impressions represents MRC-compliant viewability count. Video completions represents full video view count. Engagements represents rich media interaction count.
attributes.references: MRC Viewability Standards; IAB Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this measurement discrepancy record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change to status, resolution, or investigation findings.

attributes.name: mrc_threshold_breach_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: MRC (Media Rating Council) Threshold Breach Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the discrepancy percentage exceeds the MRC 10 percent materiality threshold. True indicates breach requiring formal investigation and potential financial adjustment. False indicates variance within acceptable tolerance.

attributes.name: primary_count
attributes.description: The metric count reported by the primary source system (ad server of record). Represents the baseline measurement for discrepancy calculation.

attributes.name: remediation_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action applied to resolve the discrepancy or data quality issue. Documents data reprocessing, manual adjustments, system configuration changes, vendor notifications, or process improvements implemented.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the discrepancy was resolved and remediation action completed. Marks the conclusion of the investigation and correction workflow.

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: Classification of the identified or suspected root cause of the discrepancy. Tag latency represents delayed pixel firing. Filtering methodology represents different data cleansing rules. Timezone mismatch represents reporting period alignment issues. IVT filtering delta represents invalid traffic detection differences. Ad blocking represents client-side blocking. Viewability criteria represents MRC viewability standard interpretation differences. Attribution window represents conversion lookback period differences. Sampling methodology represents statistical sampling variance. Technical error represents system malfunction. Unknown represents unresolved cause. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tag_latency|filtering_methodology|timezone_mismatch|ivt_filtering_delta|ad_blocking|viewability_criteria|attribution_window|sampling_methodology|technical_error|unknown — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Invalid Traffic Detection Guidelines; MRC Viewability Standards

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative explanation of the root cause analysis findings. Documents the investigation process, evidence reviewed, technical factors identified, and conclusion reached regarding why the discrepancy occurred.

attributes.name: secondary_count
attributes.description: The metric count reported by the secondary source system (vendor or publisher). Represents the comparison measurement for discrepancy calculation.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the discrepancy represents a breach of contractual service level agreement for data quality, delivery accuracy, or reporting timeliness. True indicates SLA breach requiring escalation. False indicates within SLA tolerance.

attributes.name: source_system_primary
attributes.description: Name of the primary measurement source system reporting the baseline count. Typically the ad server of record such as Google Campaign Manager 360 or The Trade Desk.

attributes.name: source_system_secondary
attributes.description: Name of the secondary measurement source system reporting the comparison count. Typically the media vendor, publisher ad server, or third-party verification vendor such as Nielsen or Comscore.

attributes.name: vendor_notification_sent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the media vendor or publisher was formally notified of the discrepancy. True indicates notification sent. False indicates internal-only issue or notification not yet sent.

attributes.name: vendor_response_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing the vendor or publisher explanation, justification, or proposed resolution for the discrepancy. Documents external party perspective and commitments.

attributes.name: vendor_response_received_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the media vendor or publisher provided a formal response to the discrepancy notification. True indicates response received. False indicates no response or response pending.

products.name: attribution_model
products.description: Configuration master defining conversion attribution models, rules, and parameters for each advertiser and campaign. Stores model type (last-click, first-click, linear, time-decay, position-based, data-driven/algorithmic, custom), attribution windows (view-through duration, click-through duration), cross-device graph enablement, cross-channel scope, lookback window constraints, fractional credit distribution weights, model training metadata (for data-driven models), and activation status with effective date range. Governs how conversion_event records distribute credit across campaign touchpoints. Model changes trigger reprocessing of historical conversions within the affected attribution window. Supports A/B model comparison and incrementality testing workflows.

attributes.name: lookback_window_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of days to look back in the customer journey when attributing conversions. Defines the outer boundary for all touchpoint consideration.

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code or identifier for the attribution model used in reporting and system integration.

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name for the attribution model configuration (e.g., 'Q1 2024 Last-Click Model', 'Brand Awareness Linear Model').

attributes.name: model_type
attributes.description: The type of attribution methodology applied: last-click (100% credit to final touchpoint), first-click (100% credit to initial touchpoint), linear (equal credit across all touchpoints), time-decay (exponentially increasing credit toward conversion), position-based (U-shaped: 40% first, 40% last, 20% distributed), or data-driven (algorithmic/machine-learning-based credit distribution).
attributes.references: IAB Attribution Standards; Google Analytics Attribution Models

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this attribution model configuration.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
